trips.title: Geography Trip to Iceland
trips.subject: Geography
overview: Iceland is an island nation in the North Atlantic, known for its progressive and peaceful society that values freedom and equality highly. It consistently ranks at the top in various global indices for quality of life, gender equality, democracy, healthcare, education, and internet access, making it one of the world's most highly regarded countries in these areas.

The country is characterized by its stark geological contrasts, earning it the nickname “The Land of Fire and Ice.” Iceland boasts some of Europe's largest glaciers as well as some of the most active volcanoes in the world.

Furthermore, Iceland is a place of dramatic variations in light and darkness. The long summer days, with nearly 24 hours of sunlight, contrast sharply with the short winter days, which have only a few hours of daylight.

itinerary.label: Day 1
itinerary.description: Upon arrival at Keflavik Airport, you will clear immigration and customs and be met by your guide and coach. Your first visit will be to Reykjanes Geopark, which lies on major plate boundaries along the Mid-Atlantic Ridge, part of the 65,000 km mid-ocean ridge that encircles the earth like the seam of a baseball.

itinerary.label: Day 2
itinerary.description: After enjoying breakfast, you will check out of your hotel. Then, your coach and guide will take you to Seljalandsfoss Waterfall, located in the southern region of Iceland. The waterfall drops 60 meters and is part of the Seljalands River that has its origin in the volcano Eyjafjallajökull.

itinerary.label: Day 3
itinerary.description: After enjoying breakfast at the Skaalin Hostel, you will visit Laki Lavas and Lomagnupur. Laki, or Lakagígar (Craters of Laki), is a volcanic fissure in the south of Iceland, not far from the canyon of Eldgjá and the small village of Kirkjubæjarklaustur. After enjoying your packed lunch, you will then visit Jökulsárlón, a large glacial lake in southeast Iceland, on the edge of Vatnajökull National Park.

itinerary.label: Day 4
itinerary.description: After breakfast, your coach will pick you up, and you will transfer to Landmannalaugar, where you will commence your full-day trip. Landmannalaugar is a place in the Fjallabak Nature Reserve in the Highlands of Iceland.

itinerary.label: Day 5
itinerary.description: After breakfast, you will take a ferry to Vestmannaeyjar (Westman Islands), an archipelago off Iceland’s south coast, formed by underwater volcanic eruptions. The youngest island, Surtsey, was formed in 1963. Heimaey is the largest and only inhabited island. You will enjoy a guided coach tour of Heimaey Island. Heimaey, literally "Home Island," is the largest island in the Vestmannaeyjar archipelago, at 13.4 square kilometers.

itinerary.label: Day 6
itinerary.description: After breakfast at your hotel, you will start a Golden Circle Tour, including visits to Gullfoss Waterfall, Geysir, and Þingvellir before heading to Efstidalur Dairy Farm. After these visits, you will have your packed lunch before heading to Þingvellir. Þingvellir (Thingvellir) is a historic site and national park in Iceland, east of Reykjavík, known for the Alþing (Althing), the site of Iceland's parliament from the 10th to 18th centuries. You will then head to Geysir, sometimes known as The Great Geysir, a geyser in southwestern Iceland. Gullfoss is one of the most popular tourist attractions in Iceland. You will then head back to Hotel Ork for dinner and an overnight stay.

itinerary.label: Day 7
itinerary.description: After breakfast, you will check out of your hotel and board the coach. You will start your day at Perlan Ice Cave and Planetarium. Full details are on their website; a brief description is below, however. https://perlan.is/ Volcanoes, glaciers, geothermal marvels, and more come alive through cutting-edge technology and groundbreaking science. The Glaciers and Ice Cave exhibition is included in this unique nature exhibition. You will then enjoy a city tour of Reykjavik by foot, where you will see the views from Perlan and the Hallgrímskirkja Parish Church. Hallgrímskirkja is a Lutheran parish church in Reykjavík, Iceland. You will then have time for last-minute shopping before heading for your last night's stop at Hotel Cabin.

itinerary.label: Day 8
itinerary.description: You will check out of your hotel after breakfast and be transferred by coach for your flight back home.

trips.title: Geography Trip to East Coast USA
trips.subject: Geography
overview: The East Coast of the USA is a vibrant tapestry of historical landmarks, cultural depth, and breathtaking natural landscapes along its extensive shoreline. Iconic cities and states immediately evoke vivid imagery, captivating the imagination of even those who have yet to visit. From the rugged wilderness near the Canadian border to the warm, inviting beaches of the Carolinas, Georgia, and Florida, the Eastern Seaboard offers a diverse range of experiences to its visitors. This region is rich with potential holiday destinations, from the historical avenues of Philadelphia and the landmark museums and government edifices in Washington, DC, to the tranquil golf courses and beaches in the Carolinas. The journey encompasses visiting notable cities such as New York, Washington, Georgetown, and Philadelphia, each offering its unique contributions to the American narrative. America's history, though relatively brief, is intensely compelling, featuring sites like the Liberty Bell and the battlefields of the American Civil War and the War of Independence. The East Coast is strewn with sites significant to the nation's past, ensuring that visitors will find their itinerary filled with enriching experiences that capture the essence of America's story.

itinerary.label: Day 1
itinerary.description: Upon arrival at John F. Kennedy International Airport, you will be greeted by your driver and transferred to your hotel for check-in. In the afternoon, you will visit the Metropolitan Museum of Art, commonly known as "the Met," the largest art museum in the United States. In the evening, enjoy dinner at a local restaurant before being transferred back to your hotel.

itinerary.label: Day 2
itinerary.description: After breakfast at your hotel, embark on a full-day tour of New York. Your day includes a visit to the Statue of Liberty & Ellis Island, featuring a boat ride through New York Harbor. Following the cruise, the tour continues to Trinity Church, also known as St. Paul’s Chapel, the oldest public building in continuous use in NYC. Next, visit the 9/11 Memorial Gardens & Reflecting Pools and the Charging Bull Sculpture, sometimes referred to as the Wall Street Bull. In the evening, enjoy dinner at a local restaurant before returning to your hotel.

itinerary.label: Day 3
itinerary.description: Post-breakfast, visit the West Point Military Academy, also known as Army West Point, The Academy, or simply The Point. This four-year coeducational federal service academy is located in West Point, New York. In the early evening, dine at a local restaurant. After dinner, visit the Empire State Building to admire the sprawling metropolis from one of the world's most famous skyscrapers, the second tallest building in New York City. Following the visit, you will be transferred back to your hotel.

itinerary.label: Day 4
itinerary.description: After breakfast, head to The Mills at Jersey Gardens Mall, a two-level indoor outlet mall in Elizabeth, New Jersey. In the afternoon, explore the Intrepid Sea, Air & Space Museum located on Manhattan’s West Side at Pier 86 at 46th Street. In the evening, enjoy dinner at a local restaurant before returning to your hotel.

itinerary.label: Day 5
itinerary.description: New York - Philadelphia - Washington DC After hotel breakfast and check-out, transfer to Washington DC, a 3-hour journey. En route, stop in Philadelphia to visit the Liberty Bell, an iconic symbol of American Independence. Then, continue to Independence Hall, a significant historical site where both the Declaration of Independence and the United States Constitution were debated, written, and ratified. Upon arrival in Washington, check into your hotel and later enjoy dinner at a local restaurant.

itinerary.label: Day 6
itinerary.description: Following breakfast at Harriet’s Diner, take a 90-minute roundtrip cruise from Georgetown along the Potomac River. After the cruise, embark on a walking tour of Washington’s monuments, including the World War II Memorial and the Lincoln Memorial, a neoclassical monument honoring America’s 16th president. trips.title: Battlefields Trip - London , France & Belgium
trips.subject: History
overview: The Battle of the Somme, also known as the Somme Offensive, stands as one of the First World War's most significant confrontations, involving the forces of the British Empire and France against the German Empire. This extensive battle unfolded from 1 July to 18 November 1916 along the River Somme's upper reaches in France. Its aim was to accelerate an Allied victory, marking it as the Western Front's largest conflict during the war. The engagement saw over three million men in combat, with casualties—wounded or killed—reaching one million, thus ranking it among the most devastating battles in human history.

The decision for a joint offensive on the Somme was made during Allied discussions in Chantilly, Oise, in December 1915. The Allies planned a series of combined attacks against the Central Powers for 1916, involving the French, Russian, British, and Italian armies, with the Somme offensive designated as the Franco-British effort. Originally, the offensive was to be predominantly executed by the French army, with the British Expeditionary Force's (BEF) Fourth Army supporting from the north. However, the initiation of the Battle of Verdun on the Meuse by the Imperial German Army on 21 February 1916 led to the reallocation of many French divisions intended for the Somme, making the British contribution the main effort.
This Battlefield tour is one among many sought-after tours available, known for their rapid sell-out due to popularity.
Our tours are customized and highly adaptable, ensuring participants gain a profound understanding of this pivotal historical episode.

itinerary.label: Day 1
itinerary.description: Upon arrival at Heathrow Airport, follow the signs to the Coach Pick-Up Point. Your coach will collect you from your designated pick-up point for a transfer to Folkestone, from where you will embark on your Eurotunnel trip to Calais. Your first visit in Calais will be to the Somme 1916 Museum, originally known as Musee des Abris. Located in the heart of the Somme Battlefields, this museum is set in a tunnel that was converted into an air-raid shelter in 1939. It recreates the life of soldiers in the trenches during the July 1916 offensive, one of the most devastating battles of the First World War, involving numerous armies of different nationalities. The museum features 15 alcoves that explore the daily life of soldiers in the trenches. A souvenir shop is available on site. After visiting the Somme, you will board your coach to check into your hotel in Arras, followed by dinner at a local restaurant.

itinerary.label: Day 2
itinerary.description: After breakfast at your hotel, you will pick up your packed lunch and board your coach to start your Somme Tour. The tour includes visits to the Thiepval Museum and Visitor Centre, Ulster Tower, Newfoundland Park (Canadian Battlefield), Delville Wood, Lochnagar Crater, and the Accrington Pals Museum. You will have some free time afterward, possibly for activities such as bowling, before dinner. Your second night will be spent in Arras.

itinerary.label: Day 3
itinerary.description: Following breakfast and picking up your packed lunch at the hotel, you will check out and board your coach for visits to the Carriere Wellington and Vimy Ridge. After the visits, you will depart to your accommodation in Poperinge to check in. Accommodations range from small hotels and guesthouses to a possible stay at Talbot House. Dinner will be enjoyed at a local restaurant.

itinerary.label: Day 4
itinerary.description: Post-breakfast, you will board your coach for a Platoon Experience Day at the Passchendaele Memorial Museum, including a road walk to Passchendaele in uniform and a Tommy Tucker Lunch. After this enriching experience, you will return to your hotel and later have dinner at a local restaurant.

itinerary.label: Day 5
itinerary.description: After breakfast, the day is dedicated to visiting Lijssenthoek Military Cemetery, Essex Farm, Vancouver Centre, Hellfire Corner, Langemark German Cemetery, among other sites. You will return to your hotel to freshen up before dinner at a local restaurant.

itinerary.label: Day 6
itinerary.description: Post-breakfast, embark on a Northern Salient Tour visiting Voormezeele Enclosure No. 3, New Zealand Memorial Park, Island of Ireland Peace Park, Pool of Peace, and Bayernwald Trenches. Enjoy some free time in Ypres for shopping, then attend the Last Post ceremony at Menin Gate, followed by dinner at a local restaurant before the ceremony begins.

itinerary.label: Day 7
itinerary.description: After breakfast at your hotel, board your coach and depart for Calais. Consider extending your trip with an overnight stay in London, where you can enjoy sightseeing, dinner at Planet Hollywood, and a West End Show at great prices.

trips.title: Geography Trip to Japan
trips.subject: Geography
overview: Japan's geography significantly shapes its society and culture due to its location and dimensions, influencing demographics, social structures, and international relations.

Known as a shimaguni or island nation, Japan comprises four major islands: Hokkaido, Honshu, Shikoku, and Kyushu, along with thousands of smaller islands, including Okinawa. The Sea of Japan sets this archipelago apart from the Asian mainland.
In terms of size, Japan is akin to the large U.S. state of California, yet it is considerably smaller when compared to the vastness of Asia and the entirety of the United States.

itinerary.label: Day 1
itinerary.description: Upon arrival at Tokyo International Airport, you will be greeted by your driver and taken to your hotel for check-in. The rest of the day is yours to start discovering the vibrant city of Tokyo. In the evening, savor dinner at one of Tokyo's many traditional Japanese restaurants. After dinner, your driver will take you back to your hotel for the night.

itinerary.label: Day 2
itinerary.description: Enjoy breakfast at your hotel before embarking on a full-day Tokyo Big Bus Tour, or opt for a Tokyo Trains pass for flexible exploration of this incredible city. Dinner will be at a local restaurant, followed by a return to your hotel for the evening.

itinerary.label: Day 3
itinerary.description: Post-breakfast at the hotel, visit the Meiji Shrine and Asakusa Temple, and enjoy a Tokyo Bay Cruise. Marvel at the views of the Tokyo bay area, including Odaiba, Tokyo Skytree, and Tokyo Tower, from the top of the ship, experiencing Tokyo's nightlife from the water. Dinner will be at a local restaurant before you head back to your hotel.

itinerary.label: Day 4
itinerary.description: After breakfast, set off for a full-day excursion to Mount Fuji, one of Japan's "Three Holy Mountains" along with Mount Tate and Mount Haku. Enjoy dinner at a local restaurant before returning to your hotel for the evening.

itinerary.label: Day 5
itinerary.description: to Kyoto Following breakfast and hotel check-out, you'll transfer to Kyoto via the Shinkansen bullet train (a 3-hour and 30-minute journey). Upon arrival in Kyoto, a driver will meet you and take you to your hotel for check-in. The remainder of the day is free for you to explore the area around your hotel before dinner.

itinerary.label: Day 6
itinerary.description: After breakfast, explore Kyoto’s Temples and Gardens, boasting over 1,600 temples. Highlights include the sprawling Zen paradise of Nanzen-Ji Temple in the Northern Higashiyama district and the iconic Kinkaku-Ji Temple, also known as the Golden Pavilion. Dinner will be at a local restaurant near your hotel.

itinerary.label: Day 7
itinerary.description: to Hiroshima Post-breakfast, visit Samurai Castle and Himeji before transferring to Hiroshima via the Shinkansen bullet train. Upon arrival, a driver will take you to your hotel for check-in. The rest of the day is free for local exploration. Enjoy dinner at a nearby local restaurant.

itinerary.label: Day 8
itinerary.description: After breakfast, explore Hiroshima. The United States incurred a total of 1.25 million battle casualties during World War II, encompassing both military personnel killed and wounded in action. Dinner will be at a local restaurant before you return to your hotel for the night.

itinerary.label: Day 9
itinerary.description: to Tokyo Following breakfast and further exploration of Hiroshima, you will return to Tokyo by Shinkansen bullet train in the afternoon. Upon arrival in Tokyo, your driver will meet you at the Shinkansen Train Station and take you to a local restaurant for dinner before heading to the airport for your return flight home.

includes: 8 nights of accommodation in a 3-star hotel.

trips.title: Barcelona Art Trip
trips.subject: Art & Design
overview: Barcelona's art and design permeate every corner, igniting creativity on every street, within each building, museum, and art gallery.
The city is dotted with Gaudí's unique creations, including Parc Güell and the still-unfinished Sagrada Familia Cathedral, Barcelona's most iconic symbol.
Coupled with the city's world-class museums and institutions dedicated to Picasso and Joan Miró, it offers an ideal itinerary for an art trip.
This remarkable city is a year-round must-visit destination, continually drawing teachers back year after year.

itinerary.label: Day 1
itinerary.description: Upon arriving at Barcelona International Airport, a driver will greet you and take you to your hotel in a coach. After checking into your pre-booked rooms, you'll have some time to freshen up before embarking on a three-hour Barcelona walking tour. The day ends with dinner at a local restaurant.

itinerary.label: Day 2
itinerary.description: Post-breakfast, visit the iconic Sagrada Familia, an unfinished masterpiece by Antoni Gaudí. Next, explore La Boqueria Market, followed by a trip to the historic Camp Nou, home to football legends. Evening activities include dinner and ten-pin bowling with friends.

itinerary.label: Day 3
itinerary.description: Start with breakfast, then head to Ciutadella Park. Participate in a 2-hour Paella Cookery workshop, then visit Park Guell and Gaudi House. The day continues with a visit to Barcelona Port and a Las Golondrinas boat trip, concluding with dinner at a local eatery.

itinerary.label: Day 4
itinerary.description: Morning at Barcelona Zoo, followed by Mount Montjuic, including a cable car ride for panoramic city views. Visit The Magic Fountain of Montjuïc, then take a 1-hour Flamenco dance lesson. Dinner at a local restaurant wraps up the day.

itinerary.label: Day 5

itinerary.label: Day 6

trips.title: Brussels Space and Science Trip
trips.subject: Science
overview: Discover Belgium, A Journey Through Science, History, and Culture Embark on an unforgettable educational adventure through Belgium, a country rich in history, culture, and scientific exploration. This carefully curated itinerary is designed to inspire young minds, offering a perfect blend of hands-on learning experiences, historical exploration, and cultural immersion. From the bustling streets of Brussels to the cosmic wonders of the Euro Space Center, this trip promises to captivate and educate students at every turn.

Starting in the heart of Europe, students will be welcomed into the vibrant city of Brussels. Here, they will explore iconic landmarks and savor the local cuisine, setting the stage for an exciting journey ahead. The adventure then takes a thrilling turn with a visit to the Euro Space Center, where students will delve into the mysteries of space science and experience the wonders of astronautics through interactive exhibits and simulators.

The exploration of scientific marvels continues with a visit to Technopolis in Mechelen, where hands-on experiments and cutting-edge technology inspire curiosity and innovation. The Museum of Natural Sciences in Brussels further enriches the trip, offering fascinating insights into the natural world and its history.

A highlight of the trip is the visit to the Brussels Planetarium, where students will embark on a breathtaking journey through the universe, exploring stars, planets, and cosmic phenomena. This immersive experience is sure to ignite a passion for astronomy and space exploration.

Throughout the trip, students will have the opportunity to experience Belgium's unique blend of historical charm and modern vibrancy. From strolling through medieval streets to enjoying the renowned Belgian chocolate, every moment of this journey is designed to be educational, engaging, and fun.

This trip to Belgium promises to be an enriching experience, leaving students with lasting memories and a deeper appreciation for science, history, and culture. Get ready for an adventure that combines learning with excitement, making education an unforgettable journey.

itinerary.label: Day 1
itinerary.description: Arrival and Exploration Upon arrival at Brussels International Airport, you will be warmly welcomed by your driver and taken to your hotel for check-in. The remainder of the day is yours to start exploring the vibrant city of Brussels. Stroll through the iconic Grand Place, soak in the historic architecture, and enjoy a delicious dinner at a local restaurant before retreating to your hotel for a good night's rest.

itinerary.label: Day 2
itinerary.description: Euro Space Center Adventure Start your day with a hearty breakfast at the hotel, then head to the Euro Space Center in Transinne. This captivating science museum and educational attraction focuses on space science and astronautics. Students will experience space flight simulators and microgravity, providing a thrilling and educational day. Afterward, enjoy dinner at a splendid local restaurant before returning to your hotel.

itinerary.label: Day 3
itinerary.description: Technopolis and Natural History After breakfast, visit Technopolis in Mechelen, a hub of interactive science exhibits. Originating from the Flanders Technology International Foundation, this attraction allows students to engage with hands-on experiments and learn about technological advancements. In the afternoon, explore the Museum of Natural Sciences in Brussels, where the wonders of natural history come to life. End the day with dinner at a local restaurant before heading back to your hotel.

itinerary.label: Day 4
itinerary.description: Brussels Planetarium Following breakfast, prepare for a cosmic journey at the Brussels Planetarium. Under a semi-spherical dome, students will experience the thrill of a rocket launch, view Earth from space, visit the International Space Station, and get up close to Saturn's rings. This immersive experience is sure to spark a fascination with astronomy. After this celestial adventure, dine at a local restaurant before returning to your hotel.

itinerary.label: Day 5
itinerary.description: Leisure and Departure Enjoy breakfast at your hotel and spend your last day at leisure. Take this opportunity for some last-minute souvenir shopping or exploring any remaining sights in Brussels before concluding your educational adventure in Belgium. You will then be met and transferred back to Brussels for your flight back to Dubai.

trips.title: English Literature Trip to London
trips.subject: English Literature
overview: London is an exciting destination regardless of your subject.

Your students will have the opportunity to witness numerous famous landmarks and historical attractions, including St. Paul's Cathedral, Buckingham Palace, and the Houses of Parliament, to name just a few.

Moreover, London is home to an array of museums and galleries, making the learning opportunities virtually endless. This city is an excellent choice for English literature because it has been the backdrop for countless literary works and the home of many renowned authors. From Shakespeare's Globe Theatre to the Charles Dickens Museum, students can immerse themselves in the environments that inspired some of the English language's most celebrated works, enhancing their understanding and appreciation of literature.

itinerary.label: Day 1
itinerary.description: Upon arrival at London Heathrow Airport, you will be greeted by your driver and transferred to your hotel for check-in. After settling in and freshening up, you will embark on a visit to Shakespeare's Globe Theater. Located on the banks of the River Thames in Bankside's Cultural Quarter, the Globe Theater is renowned for its world-class productions of Shakespeare's plays, attracting thousands of visitors every day. Following your visit to Shakespeare’s Globe, you will have some free time before enjoying dinner at a local restaurant and returning to the hotel for your overnight stay.

itinerary.label: Day 2
itinerary.description: Start your day with breakfast, followed by a guided walking tour of London. This tour offers an opportunity to see London's most fascinating and unique sites, delving into the city's rich history and diverse culture. You'll encounter numerous iconic sights along the way! After a lunch break, your next destination is the London Eye. Situated on the South Bank of the River Thames, this giant Ferris wheel stands as Europe's tallest and the UK's most popular paid tourist attraction, drawing over 3.75 million visitors each year. Conclude your day with dinner at a local restaurant before returning to your hotel.

itinerary.label: Day 3
itinerary.description: After breakfast, the day begins with a visit to the British Library, the national library of the United Kingdom and the largest national library in the world by the number of items cataloged, housing an estimated 150–200 million items from various countries. Following lunch, you will explore the British Museum in Bloomsbury, the world's first national public museum, dedicated to human history and culture. Enjoy some free time after your visit, then dine at a local restaurant before heading back to your hotel.

itinerary.label: Day 4
itinerary.description: Enjoy breakfast at the hotel and pick up your packed lunch for a full-day excursion to Windsor Castle, a royal residence located in Berkshire. Built by William the Conqueror shortly after the Norman conquest of 1066, Windsor Castle has a rich history. After a day of exploring, enjoy dinner arranged by your driver before returning to your hotel.

itinerary.label: Day 5
itinerary.description: Post-breakfast, today's adventure takes you to the Harry Potter Studio Tour. For over ten years, the Harry Potter film series called Leavesden its home. The Warner Bros. Studio Tour London - The Making of Harry Potter offers fans a chance to explore the iconic props, costumes, and sets up close, experiencing the magic of filmmaking firsthand. After enjoying lunch at the Harry Potter Studio Café, continue exploring the studio. The evening promises dinner at Planet Hollywood and a West End show of your choice, followed by a transfer back to your hotel.

itinerary.label: Day 6
itinerary.description: Following breakfast, visit Madame Tussauds, the famous wax museum founded by wax sculptor Marie Tussaud. After your visit, savor lunch at a local restaurant. Then, your driver will escort you back to the hotel to freshen up before your departure to the airport for your flight home.

trips.title: History Trip to Athens
trips.subject: History
overview: Athens, renowned as the historic heart of Europe, boasts an extensive heritage that traces back to the Neolithic era. Its zenith, reached in the 5th century BC during the "Golden Age of Pericles," marked a period when Athens' cultural and democratic values gained widespread acclaim. Throughout its history, the city was adorned by various conquerors with magnificent monuments, creating a unique tapestry of historical layers. Since being named the capital of the modern Greek state in 1834, Athens has evolved into a captivating metropolis, blending its ancient charm with modern allure. This rich historical lineage and the city's array of architectural marvels make it an ideal destination for those seeking to immerse themselves in history.

itinerary.label: Day 1
itinerary.description: Upon arrival at Athens International Airport, you'll be greeted by your driver and taken to your hotel in a private coach for check-in. You'll have some free time to begin exploring the vibrant city at your leisure. In the evening, enjoy dinner at a local restaurant before returning to your hotel for the night.

itinerary.label: Day 2
itinerary.description: Following breakfast at your hotel, your day begins with a visit to the Acropolis, situated on a flat-topped rock that rises 150 meters (490 feet) above sea level in Athens. Next, explore the Ancient Agora, the most famous example of an ancient Greek agora, followed by a visit to the Acropolis Museum. These monuments have withstood the test of time, enduring through ancient times and the Middle Ages. In the afternoon, your tour continues to the National Archaeological Museum, which displays significant artifacts from various archaeological sites across Greece, from prehistory to late antiquity. Enjoy dinner at a local restaurant before heading back to your hotel.

itinerary.label: Day 3
itinerary.description: After breakfast, you'll set off on a full-day trip to Delphi, home to the Temple of Apollo and the Archaeological Museum of Delphi. Delphi is renowned as the ancient sanctuary that became wealthy as the seat of the oracle, Pythia, consulted on important decisions throughout the ancient classical world. Following your visit to the temple, which dates back to the 4th century BC, explore the Archaeological Museum of Delphi. After an enlightening day, return to your hotel, with dinner at a local restaurant en route.

itinerary.label: Day 4
itinerary.description: Post-breakfast, embark on a full-day excursion to Mycenae and Epidavros. Mycenae, an archaeological site near Mykines in Argolis, northeastern Peloponnese, Greece, is built on a hill 900 feet above sea level, approximately 19 kilometers (12 miles) from the Gulf of Argolis. In the afternoon, the tour proceeds to Epidavros, a small city in ancient Greece located on the Argolid Peninsula at the Saronic Gulf. Conclude your day with a transfer back to your hotel, enjoying dinner at a local restaurant along the way.

itinerary.label: Day 5
itinerary.description: Enjoy breakfast and then take advantage of your last day for leisure activities or shopping. In the afternoon, you'll check out of your hotel and be transferred to the airport for your flight home.

includes: Full-day excursion to Mycenae and Epidaurus, including all entrance fees.

trips.title: Political trip to Berlin
trips.subject: Politics
overview: Berlin serves as both a city and the capital of the Federal Republic of Germany.
The President of Germany, who primarily holds ceremonial duties as outlined by the German constitution, resides officially in Schloss Bellevue.

As the heart of the German executive branch, Berlin hosts the Chancellery (Bundeskanzleramt), opposite which stands the Bundestag, the German Parliament, located in the refurbished Reichstag building since the governmental shift to Berlin in 1998.
The Bundesrat, functioning similarly to an upper house and representing the Federal States (Bundesländer) of Germany, is situated in the erstwhile Prussian House of Lords.

The capital is also home to the ministries and departments of Defense, Justice and Consumer Protection, Finance, Interior, Foreign Affairs, Economic Affairs and Energy, Labour and Social Affairs, Family Affairs, Senior Citizens, Women and Youth, Environment, Nature Conservation, Building, and Nuclear Safety, Food and Agriculture, Economic Cooperation and Development, Health, Transport, Digital Infrastructure, and Education and Research.

itinerary.description: Upon arrival at Berlin International Airport, a driver will meet you and facilitate your transfer to the hotel for check-in. The remainder of your day is at leisure, offering the perfect opportunity to begin exploring the vibrant city of Berlin. itinerary.label: Day 2

Situated in the heart of Berlin, within the erstwhile governmental quarter of East Germany and along the Spree River opposite the Berlin Cathedral, the DDR Museum offers a deep dive into the history of East Germany. The afternoon is reserved for a visit to the Bundestag Dome, part of the Research and External Relations Directorate-General of the Administration of the German Bundestag. Conclude your day with dinner at another local restaurant before heading back to the hotel.

itinerary.label: Day 3
itinerary.description: Following breakfast, embark on a tour to the Hohenschönhausen Stasi prison, established by the East German Ministry of State Security (MfS) in 1951 as a Soviet cellar prison in Berlin-Hohenschönhausen. In the afternoon, experience "Europe in Berlin" at the permanent exhibition EUROPA EXPERIENCE, promising an engaging journey through European culture and history. Dinner will be served at a local restaurant, after which you'll return to your hotel.

itinerary.label: Day 4
itinerary.description: After breakfast, your day begins with a visit to the Brandenburg Gate, an iconic neoclassical monument commissioned by Prussian king Frederick William II in the 18th century following the Batavian Revolution's quelling. Post-visit, enjoy lunch at a nearby restaurant. The afternoon will be spent exploring Museum Island, a UNESCO World Heritage Site renowned for its rich cultural and architectural heritage. The day ends with dinner at a local restaurant, courtesy of your driver, before you return to your hotel.

itinerary.label: Day 5

trips.title: Mathematics Trip to Paris
trips.subject: Mathematics
overview: Paris stands as an exceptional destination for a mathematics-focused school trip, not only for its historical significance but also for the wealth of real-world mathematical applications it offers. The city is a treasure trove of architectural marvels and monuments that embody mathematical principles, making it an ideal outdoor classroom. For instance, the Louvre Pyramid serves as a fascinating case study in geometry, inviting students to explore the complexities of shapes, symmetry, and proportions. Similarly, the Eiffel Tower can be examined through the lens of mathematical engineering, illustrating the importance of calculations in achieving structural integrity and aesthetic beauty.

Beyond architecture, Paris's role as a vibrant financial hub provides a practical context for understanding currency conversion and the mathematics of economics. The city's rich history in the development of mathematics, with notable figures such as René Descartes and Pierre-Simon Laplace having walked its streets, adds depth to the educational experience. Engaging with the city's resources, from museums dedicated to science and mathematics to interactive workshops, allows students to see the relevance of mathematics in everyday life and historical progress. This immersive approach not only enhances their learning but also inspires a deeper appreciation for mathematics in the world around them.

itinerary.label: Day 1
itinerary.description: Upon your arrival at Charles de Gaulle Airport, a designated driver will welcome you and escort you to your hotel for check-in. Once you've settled in, you'll have the remainder of the day to begin your Parisian adventure at your own pace. itinerary.description: Kick off your morning with breakfast before heading out for an exhilarating day at Disneyland Paris. Known initially as Euro Disney Resort, this enchanting theme park, located in Marne-la-Vallée, just 32 kilometers east of Paris's heart, stands as Europe's most visited theme park. After a day filled with magical moments, a driver will escort you to a charming local restaurant for dinner, followed by a return to your hotel.

itinerary.label: Day 3
itinerary.description: Post-breakfast, the day begins with a visit to The Mathematical Society of France (SMF), a cornerstone for French mathematicians. This cruise offers unparalleled views of Paris's iconic landmarks, from the majestic Eiffel Tower to the historical Notre Dame Cathedral and the Louvre, promising a memorable experience. The day concludes with dinner at a local restaurant, after which you'll head back to the hotel.

itinerary.label: Day 4

The afternoon's highlight is a visit to the iconic Eiffel Tower, a symbol of French innovation and elegance. This landmark is not just a feast for the eyes but also the most-visited paid monument globally. Dinner will be served at a local restaurant, rounding off another enriching day before returning to your hotel.

itinerary.label: Day 5

trips.title: Religious Trip to Rome
trips.subject: Admin
overview: The Minor focuses on World Religions within the context of Rome and the Mediter-ranean. Romo is the rich religious history in a cultural and religious crossroads for today's Roman Catholic Church. Professors utilize Rome as an extension of the classroom, teaching at sites like the Vatican Museums, St. Peter’s Basilica, and the Catacombs of San Callisto. On-site activities and team assignments help you learn through experience, while an Italian language course contribute to your ability to communicate. Fall semester students may choose to enroll in an optional elective course through our partner, LUISS University (LUISS).

trips.title: History Trip to Jordan
trips.subject: History
overview: The history of Jordan encompasses the development of the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan, the era of the Emirate of Transjordan under British protection, and the broader historical narrative of the Transjordan region.

Archaeological findings suggest human presence in Transjordan dates back to the Paleolithic era. During the Bronze Age, the region was inhabited by nomadic tribes, which eventually formed small kingdoms in the Iron Age, such as Edom and Ammon, with some territories being under Israeli control. The narrative of Transjordan progresses with the advent of Muslim rule in the 7th century, followed by periods of Crusader dominion in the Middle Ages (notably the territory known as Oultrejordain), and later, governance by the Mamluk Sultanate.

itinerary.label: Day 1
itinerary.description: Upon arrival at Queen Alia International Airport, your driver will meet you and transfer you to your hotel for check-in. The remainder of the day will be at your leisure. In the evening, dinner will be served at a local restaurant.

trips.title: Musical Trip to Vienna
trips.subject: Music
overview: The Vienna Music Tour presents an unparalleled educational opportunity for students, immersing them in the rich tapestry of classical music history where they can explore the lives and legacies of iconic composers such as Mozart, Beethoven, and Haydn. This journey through Vienna, the heart of classical music, not only enriches students' understanding of musical composition and its historical context but also inspires creativity and a deeper appreciation for the arts. By walking in the footsteps of these musical giants, students connect with the cultural heritage that shaped the soundtrack of history, making it an ideal educational excursion.

itinerary.label: Day 1
itinerary.description: Upon arrival at Vienna International Airport, your driver will welcome you and escort you to your hotel for check-in. Following check-in, embark on a half-day panoramic tour of Vienna, offering a glimpse into the city's majestic landscapes and historical sites. Conclude your day with a delightful dinner at a local restaurant.

itinerary.label: Day 2
itinerary.description: Start your day with breakfast at the hotel, then set off for a full day dedicated to exploring the residences of Vienna's legendary composers. Immerse yourself in the rich musical heritage that defines this city. In the evening, savor dinner at another local restaurant before returning to your hotel for the night.

itinerary.label: Day 3
itinerary.description: After breakfast, indulge in another full day panoramic tour of Vienna. This tour will introduce you to the stunning vistas and architectural marvels that dot the city. Enjoy dinner at a local restaurant in the evening, then retire to your hotel.

itinerary.label: Day 4
itinerary.description: Post-breakfast, today's journey takes you to Salzburg, the birthplace of Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart, a prodigious composer whose works have left an indelible mark on classical music. Spend the day discovering the life and legacy of Mozart. The day ends with dinner at a local restaurant in Salzburg.

itinerary.label: Day 5
itinerary.description: Following breakfast, embark on a full day tour dedicated to Vienna's musical landscape. This immersive experience will deepen your appreciation for the city's musical contributions. The day concludes with a meal at a local restaurant.

itinerary.label: Day 6

trips.title: Hue- Hoi An Heritage Tour
trips.subject: History
overview: A region of contrasts, from the refined colonial architecture in Hanoi to the dramatic tiered landscapes in the hills around Mai Chau, and the sublime beauty of the karst islands in Halong Bay, the north of Vietnam is practically a destination in its own right. It offers wonderful opportunities to meet indigenous folk in the mountains, as well as to immerse oneself in one of Asia’s most vibrant cities. Whether you are interested in the daily life of the countryside or seeking a tranquil escape from the fast-paced city life, the "Northern Vietnam Soft Adventure 8 Days" tour is an excellent choice. This tour provides a great opportunity to explore the serene landscapes throughout the northern part of the country.

itinerary.label: Day 1
itinerary.description: Arrival in Ho Chi Minh City – Transfer to Hue Upon arriving in Ho Chi Minh City, you have the option to spend the night or directly fly to Hue to start your journey. In Hue, a local guide will greet you and facilitate your transfer to the hotel for check-in. After settling in, embark on an electric cart tour to The Imperial Citadel, the historical seat of the Nguyen Dynasty from 1802 to 1945. Next, visit the Hue Royal Fine Arts Museum, located within the former Dien Long An Royal Palace. In the evening, savor a welcome dinner at a Royal restaurant featuring traditional music performances, marking your first night in Hue.

itinerary.label: Day 2
itinerary.description: Exploring Hue by Boat and Bicycle Start the day with breakfast, followed by a serene boat trip on the Perfume River to the Thien Mu Pagoda. Then, cycle to the tombs of Tu Duc and Khai Dinh, with a lunch stop at a pagoda. In the afternoon, continue biking to the Thanh Toan Bridge and through the Hue countryside. Conclude your day with dinner at a local eatery before returning to your hotel.

itinerary.label: Day 3
itinerary.description: Hue to Hoi An via Danang Post-breakfast, a private vehicle will take you to Hoi An via the picturesque Highway 1A. En route, pause to admire the beautiful landscapes of Lang Co Beach and Danang city. In Danang, visit the Cham Museum, home to the world's most extensive collection of Cham artifacts; China Beach, a popular rest spot for Americans; and Marble Mountain, symbolizing the universe's five elements. Arrive in Hoi An in the afternoon, check into your hotel, and then enjoy a walking tour around the ancient town, visiting key sites like the Japanese Covered Bridge and the Pottery Museum. Dinner will be at a local restaurant after freshening up at your hotel.

itinerary.label: Day 4
itinerary.description: Eco Fishing and Farming Tour in Hoi An Embark on an Eco Farming & Fishing Life Tour early in the morning. Starting in Tra Que Village, gain insight into local farming practices by participating in land preparation and fertilization using seaweed. Enjoy a bike tour through the countryside, experiencing Vietnamese rural life and even riding a water buffalo. Later, join a river cruise on an Eco-tour boat to see local fishermen at work and try traditional net fishing. Continue the adventure in a Vietnamese bamboo basket boat along a coconut palm-lined waterway. Lunch will feature vegetables from Tra Que Village, served on your boat. The rest of the afternoon is free until dinner at a local restaurant.

itinerary.label: Day 5

trips.title: Adventure trip to New Zealand
trips.subject: Outdoor Education
overview: On this student-centered educational trip to New Zealand, renowned for its pioneering extreme sports and stunning landscapes, participants will dive into a world of learning and adventure. Students will immerse themselves in a new culture, gaining cultural awareness while being surrounded by New Zealand's breathtaking scenery—from the rugged Southern Alps and wild West Coast rainforests to the iconic granite peaks of Milford Sound and the tropical beaches of the North, along with the country's rich indigenous history. Whether it's waterfall climbing, which caters to both novices and experienced climbers, or engaging in exciting adventure activities, students will not only enjoy the thrill but also learn valuable physical skills such as paddling, skiing, and mountain biking, enhancing their coordination. This journey fosters the development of social skills through interactions with peers, staff, and locals, and encourages students to cultivate leadership qualities by taking responsibility for themselves. Moreover, they will expand their knowledge of travel procedures and global geography, understand personal and social responsibility, and experience a once-in-a-lifetime trip that educates in the most expansive classroom: the great outdoors of New Zealand.

trips.title: Community Service trip to Cambodia
trips.subject: Volunteering
overview: Cambodia offers a profound mix of emotions and discoveries. You are transported back to the glory days of what was once Southeast Asia's most formidable empire, while also confronting the harrowing reality of a period when the Pol Pot regime led to the deaths of nearly a quarter of Cambodia's population. In the present day, Cambodia stands as a safe, inviting country, presenting an exceptional opportunity for students keen on exploring themes of development, ecology, politics, and the history of Southeast Asia. This 7-day educational excursion to Cambodia is crafted to offer students a variety of extraordinary experiences, from engaging authentically with their Khmer peers, participating in an exhilarating 'Great Race' city adventure, to learning local culinary arts through a hands-on cooking class, and the invaluable chance to interact with a survivor and former members of the Khmer Rouge Regime.

Designed with a focus on service-learning, the trip includes a rigorous service initiative where students will collaborate with villages in a secluded district to support a local community through a sustainable farming project. Above all, the trip aims to be deeply rewarding, ensuring students have a fun and unforgettable introduction to Cambodia, one of the most hospitable nations in Asia.

itinerary.label: Day 1
itinerary.description: Welcome to Cambodia! Upon landing in Phnom Penh, a driver will greet you and take you to your hotel for check-in. Settle in and enjoy a welcoming dinner at the hotel, marking your first night in Cambodia. Stay: Phnom Penh Meals: Dinner

itinerary.label: Day 2
itinerary.description: Exploring the Capital: Phnom Penh Kick off the day with breakfast before setting out 15 kilometers from Phnom Penh to the Beoung Cheoung Ek Memorial Museum (The Killing Fields), guided by your tour leader. Following this, return to Phnom Penh to visit the Tuol Sleng Museum (S21) and watch a documentary shedding light on the Khmer Rouge regime's atrocities. Pay respects at the massive Stupa, housing skulls and remnants from this dark period, erected for annual memorial ceremonies. Post-lunch, delve into Cambodian culture with tours of the National Museum and the Royal Palace, including the Silver Pagoda, admiring its unique architecture and the Throne Hall’s opulence. Cap off the day with a Cyclo ride along the Mekong Riverfront to Wat Phnom, immersing in Phnom Penh's vibrant atmosphere. Stay: Phnom Penh Meals: Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner

itinerary.label: Day 3

Meet your local guide upon arrival and proceed to Camp Tbeng in the peaceful Tbeng village, about 30 minutes from Siem Reap. After a camp introduction, check into the traditional long house and enjoy a barbecue welcome dinner. The evening includes a heartfelt talk from a landmine victim, sharing his life story. Stay: Camp Tbeng Meals: Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner

itinerary.label: Day 4
itinerary.description: Community Service at Camp Tbeng Start with breakfast at the camp before heading to a local school for a service learning program. Students will split into groups for various tasks, ranging from educational activities with local children to hands-on projects improving school facilities, guided by local experts. After lunch and a Khmer language session at the camp, return to the school to continue your service work, concluding the day back at the camp for dinner and rest. Stay: Camp Tbeng Meals: Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner

Stay: Camp Tbeng Meals: Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner

Share this meal with local students and teachers for lunch. Afterward, pack up at the campsite and head back to Siem Reap, where your evening includes an Apsara Dance Performance during dinner at Kannell Restaurant. Stay: Siem Reap Meals: Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner

itinerary.description: Discovering Angkor's Heart Discover the marvels of Angkor Thom, Ta Prohm, and Angkor Wat, experiencing the blend of historical significance and natural beauty. Enjoy lunch at a nearby restaurant and end the day with a sunset view from Bakheng Mountain or Pre Rup Temple. Dinner at a local restaurant wraps up the evening before returning to your hotel. Stay: Siem Reap Meals: Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner

trips.title: Language trip to Paris
trips.subject: Languages
overview: Take your students on a captivating adventure to Paris, the epitome of sophistication and cultural richness, with a school trip designed to ignite inspiration and joy!

Students will have the opportunity to immerse themselves in the French language at a renowned language school situated in the vibrant heart of Paris. Lessons are conducted by experienced, native French-speaking instructors, who will personalize the engaging and interactive curriculum to suit your educational requirements. To enhance their learning experience, students will also participate in diverse cultural activities, providing them with practical language application in authentic contexts.

trips.title: Space Camp Turkey
trips.subject: Science
overview: Space Camp Turkey offers an exceptional opportunity for children with an interest in space, engineering, science, or aviation to gain hands-on experience and training outside the traditional classroom setting. The camp's engaging space and technology presentations aim to guide children towards finding their career paths, inspired by stories and images of astronauts who've visited the camp.

Key life skills such as problem-solving, time management, and leadership are developed through the camp's activities. Children learn to tackle challenges creatively, manage their time effectively by distinguishing between urgent and important tasks, and pursue leadership roles, all in a supportive and team-oriented environment.

Teamwork is a fundamental part of the Space Camp Turkey experience, teaching children the value of working together through various activities like hot air balloon construction, space shuttle simulations, and mission patch creation. The camp's counselors play a vital role in nurturing these skills, encouraging collaboration, and fostering a sense of community among campers.

Moreover, Space Camp Turkey emphasizes STEM education, utilizing NASA-designed astronaut training simulators and real-world applications of scientific concepts to make learning engaging and relevant. This hands-on approach aims to inspire students to take on more challenging STEM subjects.

The camp also offers personal growth opportunities through its safe and secure environment, where children can meet new friends, take on responsibilities, and interact with adult role models like counselors. This unique experience supports children's self-confidence and personal development, making Space Camp Turkey an impactful and memorable journey towards their future careers.

itinerary.label: Day 2

Solar observation involves studying the Sun's behavior and its impact on Earth and the rest of the Solar System. Next, experience the Zero-G wall, simulating weightlessness in space. After a one-hour lunch, the afternoon includes a 3D workshop, Mission Patch Design—highlighting the symbolism and importance of mission patch elements—and the Astronaut Challenge, focusing on physical training vital for space travel. India, home to a significant number of street children living in poverty without access to adequate shelter, education, healthcare, or parental care, presents a critical area for intervention.

The Street Children Project is crafted to mitigate these challenges, relying on the dedication and enthusiasm of volunteers to make a tangible difference in the lives of these children through local shelters and informal education centers.

Volunteers dedicate their time to various tasks at these shelters or centers, including teaching, managing administrative responsibilities, and creating interactive lessons and games. Additionally, special sessions focusing on art and crafts are organized not only to beautify the centers but also to foster a deeper connection with the children.
This program is designed to offer participants an opportunity to experience India authentically and responsibly, bridging the gap between travel and meaningful contribution to society.

trips.title: India Adventure and Community Service
trips.subject: Volunteering
overview: Not all classrooms have four walls" - this statement beautifully captures the essence of real-world learning, and it's time we open the doors to outdoor learning experiences for our children. The Himalayan Community Service & Adventure Tour in Palampur is a meticulously curated journey that promises to broaden the horizons of students beyond the conventional classroom setup. Over the course of 8 days, students will immerse themselves in the breathtaking beauty of the Himalayan foothills, engage with the local community in a meaningful way, and embrace the serenity of nature while camping in the wilderness.

This tour is not just about witnessing the majestic beauty of the Himalayas; it's an invitation to live amidst it. Students will have the chance to wander through the lush tea gardens of Palampur, a serene experience that combines learning with the tranquility of nature. The adventure continues as they settle into a campsite enveloped by the raw beauty of the Himalayas, offering them a unique opportunity to soak in the purity and freshness of the environment.

A significant aspect of this tour is the community and service learning opportunity at a rural school. Here, students will not only contribute to the community through service but also learn the invaluable lesson of selflessness. They will have the chance to share their creative ideas and partake in renovating the school, making a lasting impact on the local community.

The journey also includes a visit to Mcleodganj, where students can explore the rich cultural heritage of the Tibetan community, visit the Dalai Lama monastery, and take a walk along the scenic Bhagsunag waterfalls. This experience is designed to foster teamwork and collaboration among students, allowing them to discover the joy of learning through exploration and adventure. Through this journey, students are set to enjoy their learning experience, making memories that go beyond the traditional classroom and last a lifetime.

itinerary.label: Day 1
itinerary.description: Upon your arrival at Delhi Airport, you'll catch a brief connecting flight to Dharamsala. Here, our local team will greet you and facilitate your transfer to Palampur. Once in Palampur, you'll be taken to your accommodations to settle in and rest up for the adventure ahead.

itinerary.label: Day 2
itinerary.description: Following breakfast, the local team will provide a comprehensive briefing, outlining the itinerary for the upcoming days and sharing essential guidelines for the group. Post-lunch, the exploration begins with a tour around Palampur town, focusing on its renowned tea gardens and the Tea Factory. This visit offers a deep dive into why Palampur is celebrated as ‘The Tea Capital of North India,’ complete with insights into tea cultivation and a chance to taste the freshly brewed tea. The day concludes with a return to the hotel for some leisure time and an overnight stay. Days Three to Six During these days, your students will venture to a local school on the outskirts of Palampur to undertake basic renovation and beautification projects. They are encouraged to infuse their creativity into painting the school, brightening the learning space for children from nearby villages. The aim is to make the school environment as vibrant and welcoming as possible, with our coordinators offering guidance and support throughout this process. Tasks will also include ground cleaning, gardening, and even painting murals. All necessary materials will be provided. Additionally, the group will engage in minor repair works, including toilet construction and repair, with local laborers on hand to assist. This segment of the trip is designed to foster teamwork and impart the value of selfless service. Meals will be provided throughout these days.

itinerary.label: Day 7

Nestled at an elevation of 6831 feet within the Dhauladhar Range, Mcleodganj boasts stunning monasteries, scenic landscapes, vibrant cafes, and a range of adventure activities. This hill town offers a tranquil escape from city life, with attractions including the Tibetan market, the Dalai Lama Monastery, St. John's Church, and the trails around Bhagsunag Waterfalls. The day promises an enriching cultural experience, complemented by the tastes of local cuisine like momos and thukpa. In the evening, the group will return to Palampur.

trips.title: An Australian Adventure
trips.subject: Outdoor Education
overview: Get ready for an unforgettable adventure to Australia, where education meets excitement!
This specially designed itinerary promises young students a dynamic blend of learning, fun, and exploration in one of the world's most captivating destinations.
From bustling cityscapes to awe-inspiring natural wonders, students will embark on a journey that ignites their curiosity and broadens their horizons.

The adventure begins in Sydney, a city teeming with history and culture. Here, your students will marvel at the architectural splendor of the Sydney Opera House, delve into marine life at SEA LIFE Sydney Aquarium, and uncover the stories of Australia’s past at the Australian Museum.
The excitement continues with a trip to the Blue Mountains, where they’ll learn about Aboriginal culture and explore stunning landscapes.

Melbourne awaits with its rich cultural tapestry. Students will immerse themselves in the vibrant arts scene at the National Gallery of Victoria and engage with interactive exhibits at the Melbourne Museum. They’ll also have the chance to experience the city’s famous street art and diverse neighborhoods, offering a colorful insight into modern Australian life.

The natural wonders of Australia take center stage as students venture to the Great Barrier Reef. This once-in-a-lifetime experience allows them to snorkel among vibrant coral reefs, discovering the fascinating marine biodiversity and the importance of conservation. The journey continues to the ancient Daintree Rainforest, where students will explore lush landscapes and learn about unique ecosystems.

Encounters with Australia’s iconic wildlife will captivate students, with visits to sanctuaries such as Lone Pine Koala Sanctuary in Brisbane. Here, they’ll get up close with kangaroos, koalas, and other native animals, fostering a deeper appreciation for biodiversity and conservation efforts.
This trip to Australia is not just an educational journey but a thrilling adventure that promises to inspire and excite young minds.
Get ready for an experience that combines learning with unforgettable fun!

itinerary.label: Day 1
itinerary.description: You will arrive in Brisbane late evening and will be met and after clearing customs and collecting your luggage you will head straight to the Hotel Grand Chancellor in Brisbane. This 4.5-star hotel in the centre of Brisbane features a restaurant and bar with city views, rooftop swimming pool and fitness room, plus spacious rooms with LCD TV and private balcony. Each room at Hotel Grand Chancellor Brisbane features a minibar and a work desk with wireless internet access. Most rooms have panoramic views of the Roma Street Parklands or the city. Frescos Restaurant offers modern à la carte dining during the evening and extensive buffets for breakfast and lunch. Frescos Bar & Café serves light meals and a variety of drinks, including cocktails. Guests at The Grand Chancellor Brisbane can work out in the rooftop fitness centre, with advanced exercise equipment. Hotel Grand Chancellor Brisbane is only a 15-minute walk to Suncorp Stadium.

itinerary.label: Day 2
itinerary.description: After enjoying breakfast at the hotel you will be ready for your first day. You will be collected from your hotel and transferred by coach to Wharf where you will take a 75 minute Ferry to Tangalooma Resort on Stradbroke Island. Protected and treasured, Tangalooma Resort is nature’s theme park where amazing natural encounters are just part of the everyday experience. With heaps of tours and activities on offer, Tangalooma is the jewel of Moreton Bay and islands. Activities on offer include Brisbane's best Whale Watching Cruise, ATV Quad Bike Tours, Marine Discovery Cruise, and the Desert Safari Tour with sand tobogganing, Snorkeling the Tangalooma Wrecks and so much more! The star attraction at the Resort is the unique guest activity of hand feeding a pod of wild bottlenose dolphins! Upon arrival at Tangalooma Island Resort you will be met by the representative from the Guests Services Jetty where you will collect your activity booklets and then enjoy a set menu lunch in the garden room before an afternoon and evening of activity and fun! You will start off with a one and half hour guided snorkeling tour of the wrecks of Tangalooma. The history of the wrecks of Tangalooma dates back to 1963, when a group of boat owners requested the construction of a man-made harbour just off the island. Fifteen vessels that were deliberately sunk to form a break wall for small boats also creating an amazing wreck dive and snorkel site. After this incredible experience you will enjoy some afternoon tea and muffins and have some free time to explore the area perhaps taking a beach walk or taking part in some sports activities where the equipment hire is free of charge. Early evening you will enjoy a set menu dinner in the Garden Room before watching a fascinating 30 minute presentation on the World of Dolphins at the Eco Centre on Tangalooma. You will then head to the Jetty where you will have the chance to hand feed one of the wild bottlenose dolphins that visit the shores each evening at sunset. The Tangalooma dolphins are playful creatures that visit regularly, each with their own distinctive and unique personalities. Tangalooma has a government permit to run the dolphin feeding program and has implemented very strict rules and regulations for the program. Tangalooma is often recognised as the world's best wild dolphin feeding programme. After a fantastic fun filled and educational day you will enjoy some night time activities before heading off to bed.

itinerary.label: Day 3
itinerary.description: After enjoying an early morning breakfast you will be taken on a fun filled Desert Safari. As part of this great trip you will receive a unique look into the heart of Moreton Island and then participate in the exhilarating sport of Moreton Island sand tobogganing, reaching speeds of up to 40km per hour! After this trip lasting one and half hours you will enjoy a chef selection of cookies and fruit at the coffee shop before having a Coastal Presentation with an Eco Ranger at the Eco Centre. You will then enjoy a picnic style lunch consisting of sandwiches, muffins, fruit and drinks before more fun where you will experience stand up kayaking until the early afternoon. You will then collect your afternoon tea and have some free time until dinner at around 6.30 pm and then enjoy a movie night with hot chocolate and popcorn.

itinerary.label: Day 4
itinerary.description: Today you will be leaving Tangalooma Island Resort but not before enjoying some more great activities. After your breakfast you will place your luggage in designated collection area and check out of your room. You will then enjoy an Island Explorer Bush Walking Tour with an Eco Ranger where you enjoy a guided bush walk into the National Park to learn about the flora and fauna of Moreton Island, as well as the history of the Island’s original indigenous community. In this 45 minute cruise you will witness over 100 species of fish and even dolphins, wobbegongs and dugongs. Back in time for lunch you will have some fun building your own burger with chips in the garden room. You will then enjoy some beach activities including Beach Volleyball, Tug of War and perhaps a sandcastle building competition. There will then be some light snacks before heading out to the jetty for your journey back to Brisbane for your overnight stay in the Grand Chancellor Brisbane Hotel

itinerary.label: Day 5
itinerary.description: After enjoying breakfast at your hotel you will enjoy a Brisbane City Historical Tour before heading to The Kooralbyn Valley for one night’s stay. The Kooralbyn Valley is a secluded hinterland paradise tucked away in the heart of regional Queensland’s picturesque Scenic Rim Region. Just over an hour’s drive from Brisbane and Gold Coast, guests can discover the beauty and tranquility that has historically attracted Australia’s highest flyers to holiday there. With its tranquil surroundings, ample outdoor space, and many facilities, The Kooralbyn Valley is perfect for an overnight stay and an active escape. Resort facilities include a championship golf course visited by the game’s greats, including Jason Day, Adam Scott, and Greg Norman, an outdoor pool, day spa, tennis courts, mini putt putt, volleyball courts, and dozens more exciting activities to keep guests of all ages entertained. The activities that you will enjoy here are an exciting 1.5 hours Country Farm Experience from 9:30am, where you will feed animals including sheep, learn to whip crack and throw a boomerang. You will enjoy a one hour golf buggy kangaroo tour followed by one hour bush dancing and camp fire, all followed by star gazing from 7pm onwards.

itinerary.label: Day 6
itinerary.description: You will check out of Kooralbyn Valley and enjoy the Spirits of the Red Sand program. A full day interactive guided program that combines both the Aboriginal and early colonial pioneering cultures. Starting from Dreamtime and involving all aspects of welcome to country; Aboriginal village visit, including a bush tucker educational walk, you will be guided through the old colonial settlement for a glimpse of life as it was during those early years of migration. Includes: Full day interactive tour 1.5 hour Welcome to Country Aboriginal Experience Traditional ‘painting up’ Souvenir boomerang to take home 45 mins bush tucker tour 1-hour Early Pioneers tour Educational handouts. You will then head to the Gold Coast where you check into the Voco Hotel, Surfers Paradise Gold Coast. Located in the centre of Surfers Paradise, Voco Gold Coast features accommodation with ocean or hinterland views. It is located just a 4-minute walk from the beach and is surrounded by a variety of restaurants. There are 2 outdoor swimming pools, 2 spa tubs and a fitness centre and games room. The modern, designer rooms enjoy ocean or river views and include a flat-screen TV, refrigerator or minibar and are fully air-conditioned. The en suite bathrooms are supplied with essential amenities and a hairdryer. Access to shared laundry facilities is available. You can also pay a visit to Clifford's Grill & Lounge, boasting a centerpiece ten-burner grill that our culinary talent sets alight daily to fire up fresh meats, seafood and other staple favourites grilled to mouth-watering perfection.

itinerary.label: Day 7
itinerary.description: After enjoying breakfast you will be collected from your hotel and head to the Currumbin Wildlife Sanctuary. The Currumbin Wildlife Sanctuary was established by beekeeper and floriculturist Alex Griffiths in 1947 as a small-scale tourist venture featuring lorikeet feeding displays in which tourists could participate. By at least 1953 it was known as the Currumbin Bird Sanctuary and by the mid-1950s had become an iconic tourist attraction on the Gold Coast. The place had evolved by the early 1970s to offer visitors a variety of experiences, including: the chance to see numerous bird and animal species and learn about their part in the regional natural environment; take a miniature train ride around the large site purchase souvenirs Enjoy a meal. In 1976 Griffiths gifted the sanctuary to the National Trust of Queensland (the Trust), and the terms of this exchange and its ongoing operation are set out in the Currumbin Bird Sanctuary Act 1976. The place was renamed the Currumbin Wildlife Sanctuary in 1995. It continues to be operated by the Trust as a nature-based tourism enterprise and is recognised as one of the oldest of its kind to remain in operation in the state. During your visit you will have a Glimpse behind the Scenes, A 60-minute opportunity to learn all about what happens behind the scenes at Currumbin Wildlife Sanctuary. Learn about conservation efforts for Koalas and Tasmanian Devils, explore the stories of the Wildlife Hospital on the Hospital Deck and back of House tour, and see important off display areas that are integral to running the Sanctuary. Includes a meet and greet with an Australian favourite animal. In the afternoon you will explore more of the Gold Coast on a one hour amphibious Duck tour. These tours have been designed as an excursion or education experience. They include all that the 1-hour tour offers plus additional information about boat building, engineering, Aboriginal history, geography and the environment. Tours are led by our chief engineer who will show the students how the Aquaduck was built and how it runs using both an engine and a propeller. Resources used include Aquaduck architectural Plans, images of the duck being built, and images of how Aquaducks are used today by the Army and the Australian Antarctic Division. All students have the opportunity to Captain the Aquaduck while on the Gold Coast Broadwater and will receive a certificate and sticker to commemorate their successful captaincy. You will then head back to your hotel on the Gold Coast.

itinerary.label: Day 8
itinerary.description: Today we spend a Day at Sea World with an Educational Programme included Marine Investigators. During this program, students will learn about the roles and relationships of marine animals within a reef ecosystem. Students will participate in a 45-minute lesson at Shark Bay’s underwater viewing gallery, followed by an hour Tropical Reef Snorkelling program, which includes 20 minutes in the water. Marine Investigators develops students’ science inquiry skills as they are literally immersed in the marine environment mastering basic snorkelling skills and witnessing, up close, the body features and behaviours typical to a variety of reef animals and how these species are all interconnected. Tonight, you will depart for Movie World and the Outback Spectacular THE SHOW Australian Outback Spectacular’s Heartland plunges guests into the outback with a compilation of dust and beauty, drought and rain, in a transformative arena that appears to spin, turn and shatter. Enjoy an all-new story with true Australian characters, Reg and Marg, that delves into the reality of living on the land. Embark on a vivid, spectacular and emotional ride into the heart of the Australian bush under the iconic red roof with a delicious three course dinner and drinks.

itinerary.label: Day 9
itinerary.description: Today you will check out of your hotel and have time for some more sightseeing and last minute souvenir shopping before heading off to Brisbane Airport for your flight back to Dubai.

includes: Watching the World of Dolphins at the Eco Centre on Tangalooma.

trips.title: Kenya Children Care - Volunteering
trips.subject: Volunteering
overview: This incredible volunteer journey offers you the chance to dive into various initiatives, including teaching, childcare, and community development. You'll gain deep insights into Kenyan culture and form close bonds with the local communities. To celebrate your dedication over five days of hard work, you'll embark on an unforgettable safari adventure, where you'll have the chance to observe stunning wildlife and possibly spot the iconic Big Five!

Approach this experience with an open mind and a willingness to adapt, as you'll be working in environments where resources are limited. Despite these challenges, the experience is incredibly rewarding, offering you the chance to connect meaningfully with the locals.
This opportunity is perfect for those who are industrious, ready to lead and embrace new experiences, and capable of working well within a team.
By the end of your trip, you'll leave with a profound sense of accomplishment, new friendships, and a certificate of participation, marking your positive impact and the invaluable experiences gained.

itinerary.label: Day 1
itinerary.description: Upon landing at Nairobi International Airport, a coach transfer will take you to your accommodation. The day continues with a half-day orientation led by your program coordinator, covering itinerary details, cultural insights, safety guidelines, transportation, and health advice. Later, you'll embark on a city tour of Nairobi, visiting two key attractions: The David Sheldrick Elephant Orphanage: Learn about the conservation efforts of The David Sheldrick Wildlife Trust, dedicated to rehabilitating orphaned elephants and rhinos. The Giraffe Centre: Discover the initiatives of the African Fund for Endangered Wildlife Kenya (A.F.E.W. Kenya) in conserving the endangered Rothschild Giraffe. The day concludes with dinner and an overnight stay at your accommodation.

itinerary.description: 5: These days are dedicated to volunteering at the Childcare Centre located on the outskirts of Nairobi. Your efforts will focus on providing love, care, and engagement through informal lessons, fun games, and creating a playful atmosphere for the children at the center.

itinerary.label: Day 6
itinerary.description: An early morning transfer will take you to the Masai Mara Game Reserve, a jewel among Africa's game reserves. En route, you'll stop at the Great Rift Valley for photo opportunities before continuing to Masai Mara for a picnic lunch. Your campsite in the northern Serengeti Plains is amidst one of the densest concentrations of wildlife in Africa, home to the "Big Five" and many other species. The day wraps up with an evening game drive and dinner at the campsite.

itinerary.label: Day 7
itinerary.description: After breakfast, embark on exhilarating game drives throughout the day, with a picnic lunch included. Options for the afternoon include a hot air balloon ride or a visit to a Masai Mara village (additional costs and age restrictions apply) or simply relaxing before dinner and another night at the campsite.

itinerary.label: Day 8
itinerary.description: Your final day begins with an early morning game drive followed by breakfast and checkout from the camp. You'll return to Nairobi Airport for your flight back to Dubai, with a packed lunch provided for the journey.

trips.title: Japan Art Trip
trips.subject: Art & Design
overview: Japan boasts one of the richest and most active art traditions in Asia, if not the world. It is home to some of the earliest known ceramics and the world’s oldest-standing wooden building. Japanese contemporary art also stands among the best globally, widely imitated and avidly collected. Between these chronological extremes lies a treasure trove of Buddhist temples and Shinto shrines from all periods, alongside impressive military architecture. Japan is rich in national, regional, and private art collections, reflecting a long tradition of art-historical scholarship and connoisseurship. Recently, a network of conservation and restoration labs, equipped with the latest technology for archaeological investigation, has been added. Despite the numerous wars and natural disasters that have periodically struck the country, Japanese arts can be enjoyed in extraordinary abundance. The vast majority of important pieces remain within the country.

itinerary.label: Day 1
