trips.title: Paris and Nice Language trip
trips.subject: Languages
overview: Paris, the French capital, offers many cultural activities, museums and fine-dining restaurants. There will be no shortage of these during your language stay in Paris. We invite you to the City of Light where you can learn French quickly and easily.

Learn French in Nice and experience one of France's most vibrant cities! Located on the dazzling Cote d'Azur coast - nicknamed the French Riviera - Nice enjoys an excellent year-round climate and high-speed rail connections to other key cities in France. A language course here allows you to truly experience the laid-back Mediterranean lifestyle for which southern France is so famous. The area around Nice also boasts a number of beautiful medieval villages, where you can enjoy some traditional local cuisine and put your language skills into practice - well worth a visit during your course at our school!

itinerary.label: Day 1
itinerary.description: Your journey begins in the heart of Paris with a morning visit to the iconic Eiffel Tower. Start early to beat the crowds and enjoy the climb or lift ride up to the observation decks, marveling at the city sprawling beneath you. Spend your afternoon strolling through the Jardin des Tuileries, the lush gardens that lead you from the Eiffel Tower to the magnificent Louvre Museum. Dedicate the evening to exploring the treasures within the Louvre, including the Mona Lisa and the Venus de Milo, before enjoying a dinner at one of the nearby traditional French bistros.

itinerary.label: Day 2
itinerary.description: On the second day, immerse yourself in the historical grandeur of Paris with a morning visit to the Palais du Trocadéro site, soaking in the unparalleled views of the Eiffel Tower from its remnants. Continue your journey through history to the Arc de Triomphe, standing majestically at the top of the Champs Elysées. Spend your afternoon wandering down the Champs Elysées, indulging in shopping, and savoring coffee at a café. As evening falls, find a spot to watch the sunset over the city, then perhaps catch a show at one of the theaters lining the avenue.

itinerary.label: Day 3
itinerary.description: Begin your day with a visit to the Latin Quarter, where you can feel the academic pulse of Paris among its historic universities and bustling cafés. Visit the Pantheon, then spend your afternoon on a relaxing Seine River cruise, passing by Paris's most iconic landmarks from a unique vantage point. End your day with a French language lesson to brush up on your skills, perhaps practicing what you’ve learned with fellow diners at a local restaurant.

itinerary.label: Day 4
itinerary.description: Depart Paris early for Versailles, spending your day marveling at the opulence of the Palace of Versailles and its vast gardens. Return to Paris to experience the Montmartre district in the evening. This artistic hilltop neighborhood offers breathtaking views of Paris, charming streets, and the opportunity to follow in the footsteps of famous artists who once called it home.

itinerary.label: Day 5
itinerary.description: Transfer to Nice early in the morning. After checking into your accommodation, take a leisurely walking tour of Nice, including the Old Town (Vieux Nice), Cours Saleya Market, and the Promenade des Anglais. Spend your evening enjoying Mediterranean cuisine at a local restaurant, perhaps trying a traditional Niçoise salad.

itinerary.label: Day 6
itinerary.description: Dedicate this day to exploring the French Riviera with a guided day trip. Visit the glamorous cities of Cannes and Antibes in the morning, strolling through their quaint streets and marinas. In the afternoon, discover the medieval village of Saint-Paul-de-Vence, before concluding your tour in the princely state of Monaco. Return to Nice for a quiet dinner.

itinerary.label: Day 7
itinerary.description: Start your day with a French language lesson in Nice, immersing yourself in the local culture and language. Spend your afternoon at leisure, perhaps visiting the Musée Matisse or relaxing on the beach. In the late afternoon, head to Grasse for a perfume apprentice workshop at Fragonard, where you'll create your own fragrance. Return to Nice for your final dinner on the Riviera, reflecting on the memories made.

itinerary.label: Day 8
itinerary.description: Your final day is at leisure until your departure. Depending on your flight time, take a last stroll along the Promenade des Anglais or visit any sites in Nice you may have missed. This marks the end of your journey through Paris and Nice, filled with art, history, culture, and culinary delights.

trips.title: Barcelona Language Trip
trips.subject: Languages
overview: Barcelona stands as Spain's cultural beacon, offering the dual charm of a bustling city life alongside the tranquility of a seaside resort. It presents a rich tapestry of opportunities for students to immerse themselves in Spanish culture and hone their language abilities. From the architectural marvels of Gaudi to the iconic Nou Camp Stadium, the city showcases the multifaceted nature of Spanish culture. Engaging in Flamenco dancing or exploring the Bullfighting Museum offers deeper insights into Spain's traditional practices, further enriching the learning experience.

itinerary.label: Day 1
itinerary.description: Upon arrival at Barcelona Airport, you will be greeted by your driver and transferred to your hotel for check-in. Once settled, your adventure begins with a visit to the iconic Sagrada Familia. The Basilica i Temple Expiatori de la Sagrada Familia, commonly known as the Sagrada Familia, stands as an unfinished masterpiece in the Eixample district of Barcelona, Catalonia, Spain. This colossal church, the world's largest unfinished Catholic sanctuary, was designed by the celebrated Catalan architect Antoni Gaudí (1852–1926). Recognized as part of a UNESCO World Heritage Site, the Sagrada Familia was consecrated by Pope Benedict XVI on November 7, 2010, and declared a minor basilica. Following your visit to the Sagrada Familia, you will proceed to Park Guell. Parc Güell is a stunning park system combining gardens and architectural elements on Carmel Hill, Barcelona. Designed by Antoni Gaudí for Eusebi Güell with urbanization in mind, the park is a testament to Gaudí's unique style and Catalan modernism. After exploring Park Guell, you'll return to your hotel for dinner and an overnight stay.

itinerary.label: Day 2
itinerary.description: After breakfast at your hotel, you will embark on a full day of fun at Port Aventura Park. Your driver will pick you up from your accommodation, and you will head to the theme park located in the PortAventura World Resort, about 85 km southwest of Barcelona. Port Aventura Park, the most visited theme park in Spain and fifth in Europe, offers a wide array of attractions. Initially opened in 1995 and later rebranded as 'Universal's Port Aventura' in 1998 when Universal Studios took over, the park is a hub of excitement and adventure. After a thrilling day at Port Aventura Park, you'll return to your accommodation to freshen up before dinner and another restful night at your hotel.

itinerary.label: Day 3
itinerary.description: Start your day with breakfast before setting out on foot or by public transport, using your travel card for convenience. The morning is dedicated to a 3-hour Spanish lesson at a local language school, providing a valuable opportunity to immerse yourself in the Spanish language. Post-lesson, you'll have some free time for lunch before venturing into the Gothic Quarter in the afternoon. This historic center of old Barcelona, stretching from La Rambla to Via Laietana and from the Mediterranean seafront to Ronda de Sant Pere, is a testament to the city's Roman and medieval past. Next, you'll visit the Picasso Museum, which houses an extensive collection of artworks by the 20th-century Spanish artist Pablo Picasso. The museum, located in five adjoining medieval palaces in Barcelona's La Ribera neighborhood, offers a deep dive into Picasso's genius. Following the museum visit, you'll return to your hotel for dinner and overnight.

itinerary.label: Day 4
itinerary.description: After breakfast, your day will again be spent exploring on foot or by public transport. The first stop is the Camp Nou, officially known as Spotify Camp Nou for sponsorship reasons. This iconic football stadium, home to FC Barcelona since 1957, is the largest in Spain and Europe. Following your Camp Nou visit, you'll participate in a cooking workshop, where you'll learn to prepare classic Spanish dishes. This hands-on experience culminates in a delicious lunch that you've helped create. After enjoying your culinary creations, you'll have the remainder of the afternoon free to spend at your leisure before returning to your hotel for dinner and another overnight stay.

itinerary.label: Day 5
itinerary.description: On your final day, after breakfast, you'll have some free time to explore Barcelona further or indulge in some last-minute shopping. Later, you'll be transferred to the airport for your flight home, bringing your Spanish adventure to a close.

trips.title: Community Service Zambia
trips.subject: Volunteering
overview: The program puts you in the dynamic environment of Livingstone, where you engage in projects crafted by local leaders to be ethical, impactful, and tailored to community needs.
Participants collaborate directly with these communities, facilitating sustainable and meaningful cultural exchanges that make a genuine difference.

This initiative blends community service, cultural immersion, and educational excursions. Your home base will be a mere 5 miles from Victoria Falls, a majestic Natural Wonder of the World, in a town renowned for its thrilling adventure activities!

itinerary.description: Post-breakfast, engage in a full day of sports, arts, and crafts, introducing physical education and creative expression to local children, promoting health, fitness, and nutrition. The evening will be spent reviewing the project's impact, reflecting on the positive change and community engagement experienced.

overview: Participate as a volunteer teacher in the breathtaking southern region of Sri Lanka, engaging in a rewarding program that offers English education to underprivileged children aged 6 to 15. This opportunity extends to local primary schools and includes a unique experience of working with young Buddhist monks once a week. You will employ both practical and theoretical teaching methods to assist students in mastering tasks ranging from crafting simple sentences to enhancing their pronunciation, significantly bettering their future opportunities within rural Sri Lankan communities.

In your leisure time, you're free to relax on the stunning beaches, explore the historic city of Galle, or encounter the majestic wild elephants in Pinnawella. trips.title: Japan Business Studies
trips.subject: Business & Economics
overview: Embark on an enriching 7days 6 nights journey through Japan, tailored for a group of business studies students.

Staying in high-quality hotels in Tokyo, Hakone, and Kyoto, this trip combines educational insights with cultural exploration, providing a comprehensive experience of Japan's dynamic business environment and rich cultural heritage.
In Tokyo, Japan's bustling capital, you will visit leading companies and business districts, gaining firsthand knowledge of innovative practices and business strategies.

They will have the opportunity to attend seminars and meet industry professionals, offering invaluable insights into Japan's corporate world. Alongside these academic pursuits, students will enjoy sightseeing, including a visit to the Edo-Tokyo Museum and a traditional Kabuki performance, to appreciate the blend of old and new in Tokyo's vibrant culture.
This of course subject to availability of the companies and people.
The journey continues to Hakone, known for its scenic beauty and hot springs.
Here, students can enjoy a river cruise, taking in the stunning landscapes and understanding the importance of tourism and hospitality in Japan's economy.

Traveling by the iconic Shinkansen (bullet train) to Kyoto, students will experience Japan's cutting-edge transportation system. In Kyoto, they will explore historical sites, such as temples and shrines, and engage in a guided walking tour of the city's ancient streets. Business visits in Kyoto will focus on traditional industries, such as textiles and crafts, providing insights into how these sectors adapt to modern markets.

The trip will also include cultural activities like a tea ceremony, Taiko drumming workshop, and a traditional Maiko performance, offering a holistic view of Japan's cultural richness. This unique combination of business studies and cultural immersion ensures a memorable and educational experience for all students.

itinerary.description: YOUR FLIGHTS QR1019 June 2025 departs Dubai at 2325 arrives into Doha at 2340 QR806 June departs Doha at 0235 arrives into Tokyo Narita Airport at 1855 QR803 June departs Osaka at 1830 arrives into Doha at 2320 QR1002 June departs Doha at 0055 arrives into Dubai at 0315

itinerary.label: Day 1
itinerary.description: On arrival into Tokyo Narita Airport you will go through the airport formalities and then be met by your guide who will escort you for Tokyo sightseeing and Arrive at hotel and check-in to your accommodation. Tmark City Hotel Tokyo Omori Conveniently located just a minute's walk away from Omorikaigan Station, Tmark City Hotel Tokyo Omori features simple and modern rooms in Tokyo. There is a 24-hour front desk on site and free WiFi is provided throughout the property. All guest rooms feature a 4K LCD TV, a coffee machine and a desk. Sealy mattresses are used on all beds for a comfortable stay. Tokyo Haneda Airport is a 20-minute train ride away from the property on Keikyu-Kuko Line. JR Omori Station is a 10-minute walk from Tmark City Hotel Tokyo Omori. Parking can only be reserved by phone.

itinerary.label: Day 2
itinerary.description: After enjoying breakfast your coach and guide will meet you and departure for Tokyo sightseeing. You will start your day by visiting Senso-Ji Temple. Senso-ji Temple in Asakusa, is the city's oldest and most significant Buddhist temple. Founded in 645 AD, it features the iconic Thunder Gate (Kaminarimon) and a majestic five-story pagoda. The temple attracts millions of visitors yearly, offering a serene spiritual atmosphere amidst bustling Asakusa. You will than enjoy traditional Japanese Tea Ceremony. Discover the intricate practices of the Japanese tea ceremony. Watch how your instructor prepares matcha green tea and the movements that accompany this artform. Savor traditional sweets and a cup of tea before you try to recreate the ceremony for yourself. Next you are going to visit the observatory at Tokyo Metropolitan Government. The observatories are places for visitors to deepen their understanding and interest in Tokyo and the Tokyo Metropolitan Government’s (TMG) policies while enjoying an amazing view. Imperial Palace is the next spot to explore. The Imperial Palace has served as the residential place of the successive Emperors since 1868. It contains the Imperial Residence and the Imperial Palace Complex, where His Majesty the Emperor undertakes official duties. Other major buildings in the Palace include the building of the Imperial Household Agency and the Palace Sericulture Centre, where the successive Empresses have raised silkworms following the precedent set in 1871 by Empress Dowager Shoken, Empress and consort of Emperor Meiji. The East Gardens of the Imperial Palace are located on the eastern part of the palace grounds and opened to the public. You will have dinner at local restaurant. After dinner you will head back to your hotel.

itinerary.label: Day 3
itinerary.description: After breakfast at your hotel you will be met by your guide and taken to Tokyo where your first stop will be Miraikan Miraikan is a place where we can understand the things happening in our world today from a scientific point of view, and have discussions while considering the future that awaits us. In addition to exhibitions that provide people with a chance to enjoy hands-on contact with science and technology, Miraikan's colorful line-up of offerings includes experienced based classes, and talks. Visitors can experience the technological progress of today, from simple day-to-day questions, to the latest technologies, the global environment, space exploration and life science. Your Next visit will be Kawasaki Robostage. Kawasaki Robostage is the robot showroom in Odaiba, run by Kawasaki Heavy Industries. Watch, touch and experience the Kawasaki’s state-of-the-art robotics technologies and knowledges. Setting a main concept “human-robot coexistence and collaboration,” the facility continues to display the latest robots. You will then spend some time at Odaiba and visit Team Lab Planets TeamLab Planets is a museum where you walk through water, and a garden where you become one with the flowers. It comprises 4 large-scale artwork spaces and 2 gardens created by art collective TeamLab. People go barefoot and immerse their entire bodies in the vast artworks together with others. The artworks change under the presence of people, blurring the perception of boundaries between the self and the works. Other people also create change in the artworks, blurring the boundaries between themselves and the works, and creating a continuity between the self, the art, and others. You will then have Dinner at local restaurant before heading back to your hotel.

itinerary.label: Day 4
itinerary.description: After enjoying breakfast at your hotel you will meet your guide and head to Hakone. Formed around 3,000 years ago after a volcanic eruption, the area offers stunning views of Mount Fuji on clear days. One of Wakudani's unique attractions is its "black eggs," or Kuro-tamago. These eggs are boiled in the sulfur-rich hot springs, turning their shells black and giving them a distinct flavor. According to local legend, eating one of these eggs adds seven years to your life. Visitors often hike the scenic trails and enjoy the geothermal wonders of this fascinating destination. You will then take the Ropeway to Lake Ashi. The Hakone Ropeway near Lake Ashi is a popular aerial lift system in the Hakone region. It provides breathtaking views of the surrounding landscapes, including Lake Ashi, Mount Fuji, and the Owakudani volcanic valley. The ropeway runs from Togendai Station, located on the shores of Lake Ashi, to Sounzan Station, passing through Owakudani. Visitors can enjoy panoramic views of the lush greenery, volcanic steam vents, and scenic mountains. You will also join a Lake Ashi Cruise. A Lake Ashi Cruise offers serene views of Mount Fuji and the surrounding Hakone mountains. Boarding traditional pirate-themed boats, visitors enjoy a leisurely journey across the crystal-clear waters, passing by lush shores and iconic landmarks. The cruise provides a tranquil escape with stunning natural beauty at every turn. On this day you can have lunch and Dinner at local restaurant. After dinner you will head back to your hotel.

itinerary.label: Day 5
itinerary.description: After breakfast you will be met by your coach and transfer to Tokyo station. Your main luggage will be transported separately to your Osaka Hotel Directly. You will take bullet train(NOZOMI221) from Tokyo10:00 to Kyoto12:15. You will reach Kyoto in afternoon. Your next destination will be Golden Pavilion, for a Kimono Experience. Kinkakuji Golden Pavilion) is a Zen temple in northern Kyoto whose top two floors are completely covered in gold leaf. Formally known as Rokuonji, the temple was the retirement villa of the shogun Ashikaga Yoshimitsu, and according to his will it became a Zen temple of the Rinzai sect after his death in 1408. Kinkakuji was the inspiration for the similarly named Ginkakuji (Silver Pavilion), built by Yoshimitsu's grandson, Ashikaga Yoshimasa, on the other side of the city a few decades later. Kinkakuji is an impressive structure built overlooking a large pond, and is the only building left of Yoshimitsu's former retirement complex. It has burned down numerous times throughout its history including twice during the Onin War, a civil war that destroyed much of Kyoto; and once again more recently in 1950 when it was set on fire by a fanatic monk. The present structure was rebuilt in 1955. You will have Dinner at local restaurant before checking into your Osaka Hotel. Hearton Hotel Nishiumeda Only a 5-minute walk from Osaka Station and the nearest stop for the Kansai International Airport Limousine Bus, Hearton Hotel Nishi Umeda features air-conditioned rooms with cable TV channels. Free Wi-Fi is provided throughout the entire property, including guestrooms, the lobby and the ground-floor restaurant. Namba and Shinsaibashi area are both a 15-minute subway ride away. Rooms at Hearton Nishi Umeda Hotel feature simple yet comfortable furnishings. They are fitted with an LCD TV, a refrigerator and an electric kettle. Nightwear and slippers are provided. Free wired internet access is available as well. The Nishi Umeda Hearton has a coin laundry at the basement level. The 24-hour front desk sells voltage converters, arranges dry cleaning and can store luggage for guests. The Hearton Hotel is close to a number of subway lines. From Osaka Station it takes 15 minutes by train to Universal Studios Japan, and 30 minutes to Osaka Castle. Kansai International Airport is about 1 hour away via Limousine Bus.

itinerary.label: Day 6
itinerary.description: After breakfast you will Meet your guide and start sightseeing in Osaka. Your first stop will be Osaka Exchange, Inc. renamed from Osaka Securities Exchange Co., (OSE) Ltd., Osaka Exchange is the largest derivatives exchange in Japan, in terms of amount of business handled. In July 2006 OSE launched their newest futures contract the Nikkei 225 mini, which is one tenth of the size of the original Nikkei 225 Futures contract and highly popular among Japanese individual investors. In September 2007 OSE established evening session for Stock Index Futures and Options. The trading hours is from 16:30 to 19:00 (JST. 7:30-10:00 in UTC).[3] In July 2012 a planned merger with the Tokyo Stock Exchange was approved by the Japan Fair Trade Commission.[4] Today, despite its name, trading for Osaka Stock Exchange takes place in Tokyo. You will then head to The Tekijuku building, located in the business district in Kitahama, Chuo-ku, Osaka, is Japan’s only Edo period school building of Western learning still in existence. The building, designated as a National Historical Landmark and as a National Important Cultural Asset, is currently open to the public. Tekijuku was a private school of Western learning founded in 1838 by OGATA Koan (1810-1863), who was respected as a leading doctor of Western medicine. At Tekijuku, Western medical research was pursued, achieving a number of great medical accomplishments, including a vaccination program and treatment for cholera. Moreover, from the closing days of the Tokugawa shogunate to the Meiji Restoration, Tekijuku produced many distinguished individuals who contributed to the formation of Japan as a modern state. A record of signatures of Tekijuku students (Seimei roku) lists the names of 636 people who enrolled at the school in 1844 and later. If we add the numbers of non-resident students and those who did not leave their signatures, including those enrolled before 1843, the total number of Tekijuku students is estimated to have reached more than 1,000, according to historical sources. In addition to these students, it is believed that many other people sought instruction from Tekijuku. In addition to these students, it is believed that many other people sought instruction from Tekijuku. Next activity is to go for Food sample making experience (Food sample is an original part of Japanese culture. They refer to the figures created to represent food, which are displayed in restaurant shopfronts.) You will then have dinner at local restaurant. After dinner you will head back to your Hotel.

trips.title: New York Media & Film Studies
trips.subject: Film & Media Studies
overview: Extraordinary Experiences. Experiential Education. We know that when planning a school trip, you want to do truly memorable things. You want to go somewhere where your students will be able to experience what they’re learning about while they’re there. And we have just the answer: New York City!

New York City has something for everyone—you can take your students on an educational tour, and they’ll come away with a new understanding of the world and how it works. They’ll learn about history and culture, and art, but they’ll also gain practical knowledge about how things work in society today.

And when you bring your students back from their tour, they’ll be ready to share all of their new knowledge with their classmates in ways that will leave them breathless with excitement about what’s possible in the world around us.

Whether you’re looking for an immersive tour that immerses your students in the culture and history of New York City or a more self-guided tour where they can explore at their own pace, we have something for everyone!

itinerary.label: Day 1
itinerary.description: Arrive at your hotel for the week after a long flight, take time to unpack and see the hotel. You will then experience the busy streets and constant flow of yellow taxis in New York Times Square. Take your time to look around and grab a bite to eat in Times Square. As sundown goes into nightfall you will experience the dazzling lights of the city that never sleeps.

itinerary.label: Day 2
itinerary.description: After a delightful breakfast, The coach will take you to the New York Film Academy, where you will have a morning group session. The New York Film Academy was built on the belief that practical learning and industry best practices are more valuable than years of theoretical study for students in film, media, and performing arts. After filling up on a quick lunch you will walk to Ellen's stardust diner but eating there will have to wait till later. This will be the pickup point for the NYC TV+ Movie Tour. Pick up is 2.00pm. The tour will last 3 hours. The movie tour explores iconic filming locations, from classic blockbusters to modern hits. In the evening you will experience a meal at Ellen’s Stardust Diner, where the vibrant atmosphere features singing servers and an extensive menu of American classics.

itinerary.label: Day 3
itinerary.description: After enjoying breakfast and once you are ready for the day your coach will pick you up and take you to south ferry. Arrive at The Battery and hop on the ferry which takes you to the iconic Statue of Liberty and Ellis Island. This iconic monument, a gift from France to the United States, welcomes visitors with its majestic presence and timeless message of hope and liberty. This trip will take around 3 hours. Just a 5-minute walk from the ferry drop off you can take photos with the famous New York ‘Charging Bull’. There are fast food restaurants in the vicinity to enjoy a quick lunch. After your lunch, your second stop will be MOMA(Museum of Modern Art). The coach will take you to your destination. MoMA, located in New York, showcases a diverse collection spanning from innovative 1880s European painting to contemporary film, design, and performance art, providing a panoramic view of modern creativity. Conclude the day with a show at Broadway. Broadway, situated in the heart of New York City, stands as the renowned center for theatrical experiences. Its is rooted in the central avenue around which numerous theaters cluster. This theater district is renowned for housing top-notch commercial stage productions in the United States, with its origins tracing back to the construction of the inaugural theaters in the 1700s. (Back To The Future)

itinerary.label: Day 4
itinerary.description: After a delicious breakfast you will visit the iconic Brooklyn Bridge. The principal span of the Brooklyn Bridge, measuring 486 meters (1,595 feet) in length, held the record as the world's longest until the completion of the Firth of Forth cantilever bridge in Scotland in 1890. After crossing Brooklyn bridge, you will then experience lunch at Time Out Market where you can witness the bridge from a different angle. The coach will then drive you through Brooklyn, New York where you will arrive at the Museum of Moving Art to see some mind-blowing displays. The Museum of the Moving Image in New York offers an engaging journey into the world of film, television, and digital media. Explore captivating exhibits, artifacts, and interactive displays that highlight the evolution and impact of moving images on our culture and society. This should take around 2-3 hours. The next stop in New York is Alamo Cinema which offers a delightful fusion of dining and entertainment. Situated in the heart of the city that never sleeps, this unique cinema experience invites patrons to indulge in a diverse array of culinary delights before settling in for a captivating movie.

itinerary.label: Day 5
itinerary.description: After a lovely breakfast, your driver will take you directly to the Highline. Arrive at the Highline to take some memorable photos and sketches of New York from above. The High Line is a unique elevated park in New York City, repurposed from an old railway line. It stretches over 1.45 miles through Manhattan's West Side, offering visitors a serene escape with gardens, pathways, and art installations elevated above the city streets. This adaptive reuse project provides a distinctive perspective of the city's architecture and the Hudson River while blending nature and urban design. Your next destination is the David Zwirner Art Gallery, which is close to the end of the highline, you'll have the opportunity to experience the exhibition 'I Spend Each Day Embracing Flowers'. Immerse yourself in the artistic beauty and creativity this renowned gallery has to offer. Or Radio City Hall Tour, The Radio City Music Hall tour is a captivating journey through the iconic venue in New York City. With access to behind-the-scenes areas, it offers a glimpse into the world of entertainment and show business. Since Jekyll and Hyde has closed its doors in New York, we have found an alternative restaurant which is Juniors Restaurant & Bakery. After eating at Juniors, the coach will take you home for a good night's rest

itinerary.label: Day 6
itinerary.description: NBC studio Tour. NBC is currently closed but will open in the short future. The NBC Studio Tour in New York offers a fascinating behind-the-scenes look at the production of popular TV shows. Visitors explore iconic sets and learn about TV production. Live-Tapings are not allowed for people under the age of 16. Following your morning experience, your next destination is the iconic Empire State Building, a quintessential structure of New York. While there might be an approximate 30-minute queue before you ascend the building, the wait is certainly worthwhile. Once at the top, take advantage of your free time to soak in the breathtaking panoramic views of New York City from its elevated heights. As you arrive at The Broadway Theatre, you'll witness the dazzling lights that emanate from its facade, setting the stage for an unforgettable experience. Prepare to be captivated by a sensational show that promises to leave an indelible mark on your memory. The magic of the theater comes to life before your eyes, ensuring a performance that you won't soon forget. (& Juliet)

itinerary.label: Day 7
itinerary.description: After an enjoyable breakfast at the hotel, your first stop of the day is New York University(NYU), where an insightful tour awaits. Discover the nuances of this prestigious American university as you explore its campus and learn about its history, programs, and vibrant student life. The next leg of your journey will take you on a short bus ride to the globally renowned destination, Macy's. Before heading into Macy’s, a quick stop at New York’s brand-new Harry Potter Exhibition, where the Wizarding world comes true. This should take around 60-90 minutes. Macys just a 4-minute walk away is a world-famous establishment that needs no introduction. Upon arrival, you'll have the luxury of free time to enjoy. Treat yourself to explore the plethora of shopping options that Macy's offers. In the evening you immerse yourself in the realm of music history and culture as you enter the doors of the Hard Rock Cafe. Be surrounded by its distinctive collection of rock memorabilia that stands as a testament to the genre's enduring legacy

itinerary.label: Day 8
itinerary.description: After delicious breakfast, you will check out from your hotel, Store your luggage with the hotel or on the coach and make the most of your remaining hours to savor the last moments of your New York adventure. Your coach will transport you to Central Park to behold its scenic beauty. This expansive green oasis provides an ideal setting to capture breathtaking visuals, film captivating scenes, and create memorable photographs and sketches. Enjoy the tranquil ambiance and the diverse landscapes that Central Park offers, providing a fitting finale to your New York journey. Indulge in an early dinner at a traditional American restaurant, savoring a final taste of uthentic American cuisine. Following this delightful meal, take a leisurely stroll back to your hotel. Retrieve your luggage and prepare for your onward journey as transfers to JFK Airport await you. This marks the conclusion of your memorable trip, filled with experiences that have captured the essence of New York City

trips.title: London Film & Drama Trip
trips.subject: Film & Media Studies
overview: This is an introduction to Film, Moving Image and Animation as forms of communication and artistic expression. The course covers a range of handmade and digital processes used to create moving images, build worlds, and tell stories.

Students will learn about all elements of production, from the initial concept through to the completed piece of moving image content with sound. We will study historical and contemporary movements, watch and discuss films, visit exhibitions, explore the outdoors, write, draw, record, imagine and create!

All projects will use primary and secondary research to inform conceptual and material experimentation. Possible outcomes are narrative and experimental short films and animations, documentaries, music videos and multimedia installations.

Media studies trips to London offer a range of exciting opportunities to inspire the next generation of media professionals. London is a great budget destination packed with lots of opportunities for educational value and unforgettable experiences for your group to immersive themselves in the media world.

There are many experiences in London when booking a media studies trip. Enjoy the cinematic experience, indulge in the world of television at ITV Daytime Studios and visit the London Film Academy for a behind-the-scenes look at the film and theatre industry. A theatre trip to the West End show in the evening is also a must!

itinerary.label: Day 1
itinerary.description: Morning: 11:30: Drop off your luggage at the hotel before making your way to Covent Garden to engage in a Private Walking Tour, a must-do experience that highlights the key attractions of Westminster. This tours offer valuable insights into the city's highlights, film locations and performing arts scene. Afternoon: After a Lunch near Leicester square its time for… The Theatre Royal Drury Lane Tour: 14:00 - this has been a site for entertainment since 1663 and is the world's oldest theatre site in continuous use. The guided tours are conducted in English and have an approximate duration of 1 hour each. Occasionally, adjustments to the route might be necessary due to concurrent events within the premises. Participants should be aware that this walking tour involves navigating several steps and exploring backstage locations. Therefore, it is advisable to wear comfortable footwear. It's worth noting that the Theatre Royal Drury Lane functions as a live theatre, which may lead to variations in the tour route. Evening: 19:00: Step into the majestic world of "The Lion King" at the Lyceum Theatre, London. Watch Simba's epic journey unfold through incredible puppetry, vibrant costumes, and the iconic soundtrack. With breathtaking visuals, unforgettable characters, and the Circle of Life, this theatrical masterpiece is a roaring adventure that will captivate the hearts of kids and leave them enchanted. Don't miss the magic!

itinerary.label: Day 2
itinerary.description: Morning: 10:00: After breakfast you will go straight to the Shakespeare Globe Tour, which provides fascinating insights into the history of theatre. Explore the reconstructed Globe Theatre, which serves as a modern version of the original, constructed in 1599 by the company Shakespeare was part of. Learn about its history, including the fire damage in 1613 and its closure in 1642, followed by the unveiling of a contemporary reconstruction in 1997. 11:30 & 11.45: Enjoy a pleasant 17-minute walk to the National Theatre, a renowned publicly funded performing arts institution in the UK. It shares its esteemed status with the Royal Shakespeare Company and the Royal Opera House, holding the title of the National Theatre of Great Britain on a global scale. Partake in the National Theatre Tour, offering an inside look at London's remarkable national theatre. The group will be split into two group 15 minutes apart.Afternoon: Immerse yourself in the treasures of the British Museum, a world-renowned institution located in London. Established in 1753 and open to the public since 1759, the museum's mission is to showcase a diverse array of art and artifacts spanning various cultures, civilizations, and historical epochs. Evening: 18:40 – 19:30 - River Cruise (arrive 30 minutes early). 20:00 – London Eye, arrive 30 minutes early. As the day progresses, walk to the London Eye and the Jubilee Gardens. At 6:00 PM, experience the magic of London with a combined London Eye and River Cruise tour. Begin by rising above the city on the London Eye, offering breathtaking views of famous landmarks. Then, embark on a peaceful boat ride along the River Thames, where you'll encounter historic spots like Tower Bridge and the Tower of London. This special journey combines the thrill of soaring above the city with the tranquility of sailing on the river, providing a wonderful way to discover London's beauty.Conclude your memorable day in London with a late evening walk back to the hotel, allowing you to savor the day's experiences before a well-deserved rest.

itinerary.label: Day 3
itinerary.description: Morning: Start your day with breakfast, setting the stage for another early start filled with exciting experiences.Begin your morning with a royal touch by visiting Buckingham Palace, the official residence of the British monarch in London. Witness the Changing of the Guard ceremony at 10:45 AM, a captivating display where guards in striking red uniforms exchange duties with precision. Capture stunning photos of the palace's gates and the lively march of guards accompanied by a military band.Late Morning/Early Afternoon: After the ceremony, take time to explore nearby parks: Relax at St. James's Park, a peaceful haven featuring a serene lake and charming pelicans.Discover Green Park's serene paths and iconic trees, providing the perfect setting for a quiet stroll.If your schedule allows, venture to Hyde Park for more open spaces and the picturesque Serpentine Lake. This morning combines royal tradition, palace elegance, and the natural beauty of London's parks, offering a delightful London experience. Afternoon: 15:00: "Back to the Future: The Musical" in London is a high-energy stage adaptation of the iconic 1985 film. Featuring dazzling effects, catchy songs, and the beloved story of Marty McFly's timetraveling adventure with Doc Brown, it's a thrilling theatrical experience for all ages. Adelphi Theatre. Evening: 19:00: Experience the magic of "Six the Musical" at Vaudeville Theatre in London! Join the six fierce and fabulous Tudor queens as they take the stage in this electrifying pop concert. With catchy tunes, history, and a royal dose of girl power, it's a must-see show for kids!

itinerary.label: Day 4
itinerary.description: Morning- 8:30-17:00- Harry Potter Studios: Begin your day with an early morning breakfast, fueling up for a day filled with wizardry and shopping. A bus will pick you up from your accommodation to take you to the Wizarding world where you can experience the magic firsthand. This studio tour, located in Watford just outside of London, offers an immersive experience that takes you behind the scenes of the Harry Potter film series. Here's what you can expect during the tour: •Explore Iconic Sets: Delve into meticulously crafted sets from the Harry Potter movies, Including the Great Hall, Dumbledore's office, Diagon Alley, the Gryffindor common room, and more. •See Real Props and Costumes: Get up close to real props, costumes, and magical objects used in the films, appreciating the intricate details that bring the Wizarding world to life. •Discover Special Effects: Gain insight into the movie magic that brought spells, creatures, and flying broomsticks to life through interactive exhibits that unveil the secrets behind these special effects. •Board the Hogwarts Express: Step onto the platform at Platform 9¾ and even board the iconic Hogwarts Express train. •Visit Privet Drive: See the exterior of 4 Privet Drive, where Harry's journey began before he discovered he was a wizard. Shop for Souvenirs: The attraction boasts a large gift shop with a wide array of Harry Potter merchandise, ranging from wands and robes to magical sweets. Conclude your magical journey at Hogwarts School of Wizardry and make your way back through platform 9¾. Your coach will be waiting to take you into the city centre. Afternoon: Proceed to Kings Cross where the bus will drop you off. King's Cross Station, a major railway station in Central London, is known for its historical significance and cultural references, including the famous "Platform 9¾" from the Harry Potter series. Evening: 19:30: After Kings Cross, a walk to the Theatre Café Diner, a unique establishment located at 154 Shaftesbury Avenue. Nestled in the heart of London's bustling theater district, it's not your ordinary restaurant. This special place combines two elements: food and theater! It offers a distinctive experience where you can savor delicious cuisine, listen to captivating songs, and feel like you're part of the thrilling world of theater. A visit of Covent gardens after meal, then wind down your evening by walking back to the hotel, allowing you to relax and recharge for the days ahead.

itinerary.label: Day 5
itinerary.description: Morning: 9:00-12:00: City Academy's not-to-be-missed theatre musical workshop! In this immersive experience, kids will spend 3 hours singing, dancing, and performing their favorite musicals. With expert guidance, participants will refine their vocal and dance abilities in a supportive and engaging atmosphere. It's the perfect journey into the enchanting world of theatre, where passion meets performance. Afternoon: 14:00 & 16:00 – Split into two groups. It’s time to embark on a Old London Underground Station Tour with London Transport Museum. Join an expert guide for a fascinating walking tour of the world's oldest underground system. Learn about the history of the 'Tube' as you journey through time, visiting one of London's earliest, original stations and its newest and most futuristic additions. Evening: 19:30: Embark on a laughter-filled adventure with "Mrs. Doubtfire" at Shaftesbury Theatre, London. Join the hilarious chaos as Daniel Hillard transforms into the lovable Scottish nanny to stay close to his kids. With heartwarming moments and sidesplitting comedy, this familyfriendly musical is a delightful treat for kids and parents. Get ready for a joyous and heartwarming experience!

itinerary.label: Day 6
itinerary.description: Morning: 9:00-12:00 Unlock the world of stage combat with the thrilling Stage Combat Workshop at Actors Doors Studio! This dynamic experience goes beyond traditional acting, offering an exciting blend of skill development and pure fun. Led by seasoned instructors, the workshop empowers kids to master the art of stage combat in a safe and controlled environment. After finishing the workshop take a walk around Whitechapel. Afternoon: 13:00: Sky Garden in London is a unique public space located atop the Walkie Talkie building, offering panoramic views of the city. This lush, landscaped garden spans three floors and features an open-air terrace, stylish restaurants, and bars. Free to visit, it's a tranquil oasis in the heart of London, blending urban architecture with vibrant greenery and providing an unmatched viewing experience. Late Afternoon: Take a leisurely stroll around Trafalgar Square. Initially built to honor the Battle of Trafalgar, this square has evolved into a versatile space for various activities, including celebrations, protests, political events, art exhibitions, and more. Evening: Collect your luggage from the hostel or hotel, and await your airport transfers. This marks the end of your trip, ensuring a smooth transition to your departure

trips.title: Singapore Business Studies
trips.subject: Business & Economics
overview: Singapore is designed to build leadership skills, develop understanding of business and gain cross-cultural insight. Typical itineraries are made up of a combination of local company visits, engaging workshops and exploring the incredible nation of Singapore.

By travelling with us, students will build 21st century leadership skills that can serve them in their futures. Students come to appreciate the diversity of Singapore and what it means to “be Singaporean” in an ethnically, religiously, and culturally diverse nation, pushing their understanding of both the existence of deep commonalities as well as the value of difference. Our MBA trip in Singapore will give students an understanding of the micro and macro economy in the region they are visiting, and our excursion-based learning experiences are designed to allow students to observe economic and business practices.
Discover a detailed itinerary trip in Singapore below! But remember, all of our trips are completely customisable.
View all of our Singapore school trips or our business school trips which are located in a range of countries.

itinerary.label: Day 1
itinerary.description: After taking the overnight Friday evening flight you will arrive early morning on 08 February feeling fully refreshed, this flight gives you maximum time in Singapore. You will complete all of the Airport formalities, and then meet your personalized coach for your transfer to your accommodation.

itinerary.label: Day 2
itinerary.description: After enjoying breakfast at your hotel you will be collected by your coach driver and transfer to one of the major companies in Singapore. Once the itinerary has been agreed we will contact the company(s) to ask them for a visit.These visits will provide you with invaluable insights into the operations, strategies, and cultures of some of the world’s leading businesses. By observing and interacting with professionals in their work environments, you will gain a deeper understanding of real-world business practices, which will greatly complement your theoretical knowledge. The visits are subject to the availability of the company. After a very enjoyable ay learning abour the business prcatices of leaing worrl companies you will enjoy inner before heaing back to your hotel accommodation.

itinerary.label: Day 3
itinerary.description: Today is a fun day! After enjoying breakfast at your hotel you will meet your coach and be driven to Sentosa Island for a full day of many different activities and fun. Spending a full day at Sentosa Island offers a rich and diverse experience, perfect for groups looking to combine fun and adventure. Start your day with a visit to Universal Studios Singapore, where thrilling rides and themed attractions can easily fill half your day. Universal Studios Singapore is a treasure trove of exhilarating rides that will leave you breathless with excitement. Get ready to embark on a wild journey through the thrilling Revenge of the Mummy, an indoor roller coaster that combines heart-pounding drops, sudden twists, and immersive special effects. For adrenaline junkies seeking an adrenaline rush, Battlestar Galactica: Human vs. Cylon offers an epic dueling roller coaster experience like no other. Feel the wind in your hair as you soar through loops, inversions, and high-speed twists. Brace yourself for a wet and wild adventure on Jurassic Park Rapids Adventure, where you'll navigate treacherous river rapids amidst prehistoric creatures. Hold on tight as you plummet down a towering waterfall! For a dose of fun, don't miss out on Madagascar- a Crate Adventure, an enchanting boat ride that takes you through the vibrant world of your favorite Madagascar characters. Universal Studios Singapore is a realm of non-stop entertainment, offering an array of thrilling rides that will make your heart race and your spirits soar. Get ready to create memories that will last a lifetime as you dive into the magical world of Universal Studios Singapore! Having spent most of the day at Universal Studios you can embark on the unique Singapore Cable Car experience where you can get picture perfect views of Singapore from a different perspective as you climb aboard the unique Singapore Cable Car. Relish 360-degree views of the city's southern precinct as you soar high above the scenic highway. Fly high above the hill of Mount Faber and through a skyscraper to cross the harbor. Look for dolphins down below at Adventure Cove Waterpark at Resorts World Sentosa Singapore. You can also pay a visit to the Sentosa Cable Car Museum and see the world's largest cable car cabin made out of Lego! As the evening approaches buy some dinner before discovering the enchanting spectacle of the "Wings of Time" show in Singapore, an immersive multimedia experience that unfolds against the picturesque backdrop of Sentosa's Siloso Beach. As the sun sets, the open-air theater comes alive with a mesmerizing fusion of lights, water, and music. Be transported on a captivating journey through time and fantasy. From dazzling special effects to intricate choreography, each scene unfolds with breathtaking beauty and precision, captivating viewers of all ages. As the show draws to a close, bask in the magic of the moment and reflect on the timeless themes of courage, friendship, and adventure. There is so much to do and see on Sentosa you may want two days! After a long but thoroughly enjoyable and fun day your coach will be waiting to take you back to your hotel.

itinerary.label: Day 4
itinerary.description: After enjoying breakfast at your hotel your coach will meet you. Your first visit today will be Block 71, Singapore’s innovation and startup hub, is a dynamic center for entrepreneurial activity. Located in the Ayer Rajah industrial estate, it provides an ideal environment for tech startups to launch and grow their ventures. Established through collaboration between the National University of Singapore (NUS), the Media Development Authority (MDA), and Singtel Innov8, Block 71 was initially focused on media and technology startups. Over time, it has expanded to include a diverse range of tech industries and innovation-driven enterprises. Block 71 offers co-working spaces, incubators, accelerators, meeting spaces, and technical resources to support startups. These facilities foster collaboration, provide mentorship, and offer access to essential infrastructure for tech development. The vibrant community at Block 71 encourages networking and knowledge exchange. Regular events, such as meetups, hackathons, and seminars, provide opportunities for startups to connect with peers, mentors, and potential investors. Visitors can participate in guided tours, workshops, talks, and mentorship sessions to learn about startup culture, innovation strategies, and practical aspects of entrepreneurship. These activities offer insights into real-world startup operations and success stories. Block 71 has nurtured several successful startups that have made significant impacts locally and globally, including Carousell, ShopBack, and PatSnap. A visit to Block 71 provides inspiration, practical learning opportunities, and networking connections for students and aspiring entrepreneurs alike. It offers a glimpse into the vibrant startup ecosystem driving innovation in Singapore. You will not be anything but inspired after this very interesting and educational visit. You will then buy lunch before embarking on a visit to the National Museum of Singapore. The National Museum of Singapore, established in 1887, is the oldest museum in Singapore. It offers visitors a comprehensive journey through the nation's history and cultural heritage. The museum is housed in a beautifully restored neoclassical building, combining traditional architecture with modern amenities. Inside, visitors can explore various galleries and exhibitions that cover different periods of Singapore's history. The Singapore History Gallery is a highlight, offering a chronological narrative of the nation's development from its early days as a trading port to its present-day status as a global metropolis. Interactive displays, multimedia presentations, and historical artifacts bring the past to life, providing an immersive learning experience. Other galleries include Modern Colony, which focuses on life in Singapore during the 1920s and 1930s, and Growing Up, which offers a nostalgic look at childhood in Singapore from the 1950s to the 1970s. The museum also houses the Goh Seng Choo Gallery, featuring a collection of natural history drawings and specimens. In addition to its permanent exhibitions, the National Museum of Singapore hosts temporary exhibitions, workshops, film screenings, and cultural performances throughout the year. These events offer visitors opportunities to delve deeper into specific aspects of Singapore's history and culture, as well as to engage with contemporary issues and perspectives. A visit to the National Museum of Singapore provides a comprehensive understanding of the nation's past, present, and future. It is a place where visitors can learn, reflect, and appreciate the rich cultural heritage and diverse history of Singapore. After a very interesting day you will enjoy dinner at a local restaurant before heading back to your hotel.

itinerary.label: Day 5
itinerary.description: After enjoying breakfast your coach will meet you and take you to the National University of Singapore. The National University of Singapore (NUS) is a leading global university located in Singapore. Established in 1905, it is the oldest higher education institution in the country. NUS consistently ranks among the top universities worldwide, renowned for its academic excellence, innovative research, and diverse student body. Offering a wide range of undergraduate and graduate programs across various disciplines, NUS is committed to nurturing future leaders and contributing to societal progress through education, research, and service. With state-of-the-art facilities, world-class faculty, and a vibrant campus community, NUS provides students with an exceptional learning environment to pursue their academic and personal aspirations. A visit to NUS provides students with opportunities to gain insights into academic excellence and research in business studies. With a visit to NUS students can to benefit from these opportunities and enhance their understanding of business studies. You will then explore Chinatown and Little India. This tour will help you understand the multi-cultural aspects of Singapore Chinatown and Little India which are vibrant cultural enclaves in Singapore, each offering a unique glimpse into the city-state's diverse heritage. Chinatown is characterised by its bustling streets lined with traditional shophouses, temples, and vibrant markets. Visitors can explore historical landmarks like the Buddha Tooth Relic Temple and sample authentic Chinese cuisine at local eateries. In contrast Little India is a bustling neighborhood known for its colorful streets, aromatic spice shops, and bustling markets. Visitors can immerse themselves in the sights, sounds, and flavors of Indian culture, from ornate temples like Sri Veeramakaliamman Temple to traditional clothing stores and street-side stalls selling Indian snacks and sweets. Both neighborhoods offer rich cultural experiences and are must-visit destinations for tourists and locals alike. You can even sample some of the cuisine for your lunch! After this very interesting tour have some free time before embarking on a Night Safari. The night safari offers a unique and enchanting wildlife experience unlike any other. As the world's first nocturnal zoo, it allows visitors to observe fascinating nocturnal animals in their natural habitats under the cover of darkness. Set within a lush rainforest environment, the Night Safari features a diverse range of animal species, including rare and endangered creatures such as tigers, Asian elephants, and Malayan tapirs. You can embark on guided tram rides or explore walking trails to encounter a variety of animals from different regions of the world, ranging from fierce predators to elusive nocturnal creatures. Special nightly shows and performances add to the excitement, providing educational insights into the behaviors and adaptations of the animals. The Night Safari also emphasizes conservation and education, promoting awareness about the importance of preserving wildlife and their habitats. Through immersive experiences and informative exhibits, visitors gain a deeper understanding of the delicate balance of nature and the efforts needed to protect endangered species. With its captivating atmosphere and unforgettable encounters with wildlife, the Night Safari offers a magical journey into the nocturnal world, making it a must-visit destination for nature enthusiasts and animal lovers alike. You will then enjoy dinner at a local restaurant before heading back to your hotel.

itinerary.label: Day 6
itinerary.description: After enjoying breakfast at your hotel your coach will meet you and take you to the iconic and world famous Raffles Hotel. Raffles Hotel holds a distinguished place in Singapore's history and culture, tracing its origins back to the late 19th century. Established in 1887 by Armenian hoteliers, the Sarkies Brothers, the hotel quickly became an iconic symbol of luxury and elegance in colonial Singapore. Its namesake, Sir Stamford Raffles, the founder of modern Singapore, inspired the hotel's name, reflecting its connection to the city's heritage. Over the years, Raffles Hotel has welcomed an illustrious array of guests, including royalty, dignitaries, celebrities, and literary figures. Its grand colonial architecture, lush tropical gardens, and impeccable service have made it a beloved institution, earning it a reputation as the "Grand Dame of Singapore." Today, Raffles Hotel continues to enchant visitors with its timeless charm and cultural significance. Students visiting Raffles Hotel can immerse themselves in its rich heritage through a variety of activities: Embark on a guided tour of the hotel to learn about its storied past, architectural features, and famous guests. Explore iconic landmarks like the Palm Court, Grand Lobby, and Long Bar, while hearing captivating stories and anecdotes from its history. Take time to appreciate the cultural heritage of Raffles Hotel by strolling through its lush gardens, admiring its colonial architecture, and soaking in the ambiance of its historic spaces. Capture the timeless beauty of the hotel through photography or artistic expression. Browse through the hotel's boutique shops to discover unique souvenirs, luxury goods, and artisanal products that reflect the elegance and heritage of Raffles Hotel. From bespoke gifts to fine jewelry, there's something for everyone to treasure as a memento of their visit. Your students will gain a deeper appreciation for the history, culture, and hospitality of Raffles Hotel, while experiencing the timeless elegance and luxury that have made it an enduring symbol of Singapore's heritage. After a thoroughly interesting morning you will embark on a Singapore Cooking Class. For a unique culinary experience, students can participate in specialty cooking classes that focus on specific aspects of Singaporean cuisine, such as Peranakan or Nyonya cuisine, Malay cuisine, or Chinese dim sum making. These classes offer a deeper dive into the cultural and historical background of each cuisine, along with hands-on cooking instruction. Many cooking schools and culinary organizations in Singapore offer customized cooking programs for groups, allowing students to tailor their culinary experience based on their interests, dietary preferences, and skill levels. These programs may include team-building activities, competitive cooking challenges, or themed cooking parties. By participating in a cooking class in Singapore, students can not only learn valuable cooking skills but also gain a appreciation for the cultural heritage, diversity, and flavors of Singaporean cuisine. It's a fun and interactive way to explore the local food scene while immersing oneself in Singapore's culinary culture. After a fun afternoon you will have some free time before heading back to your hotel to freshen up and change and enjoy your last dinner at a local restaurant.

itinerary.label: Day 7
itinerary.description: Today is the last day of your trip and after enjoying breakfast at your hotel you will check out by 1100 am and store your luggage whilst you embark on your last day of activity. Start by heading to Orchard Road where there are many shops and malls catering to all budgets. For students a great place is East Plaza a shopping mall popular among young locals and tourists for its affordable fashion and streetwear. With multiple levels of shops selling everything from clothing and shoes to accessories and gadgets, it's a great place to score trendy finds at bargain prices. Alternatively take a wander round Bugis Street a bustling street market known for its affordable fashion finds and trendy accessories. With hundreds of stalls selling clothing, shoes, bags, and accessories at wallet-friendly prices, it's a favorite shopping destination for budget-conscious young shoppers. Another great are for students is Haji Lane in the Kampong Glam neighborhood a hip and eclectic shopping street lined with independent boutiques, vintage shops, and quirky cafes. Here, young shoppers can find unique fashion pieces, handmade crafts, and trendy accessories that won't break the bank. You will then head back to your hotel, collect your luggage and board your coach for your flight back to Dubai at 2100
